Sales OS design system

Components

  • Button (.md): Button runs one action on the current screen when pressed, such as saving a form, recording a payment or opening a menu.
  • Checkbox (.md): Checkbox lets someone turn one option on or off, or pick several options from a list, where each choice stands on its own.
  • DataTable (.md): DataTable lists records of one kind so someone can scan them, sort by a column, page through them and open one.
  • EmptyState (.md): EmptyState tells someone why a list, panel or section has nothing in it and what would fill it.
  • EntityDrawer (.md): EntityDrawer shows one record, such as a customer, sale, product or supplier, beside the list it was opened from, with that record's iden...
  • FilterBar (.md): FilterBar narrows the list under it: a search box, a few inline filters, a "More filters" panel for rare ones, the active filters as remo...
  • FilterSelect (.md): FilterSelect picks one value from a short fixed list, as a list filter or as a form field, in an in-app menu that follows the theme.
  • OverflowMenu (.md): OverflowMenu holds the secondary and destructive actions of a page, a record or a row behind one ⋯ button, so the primary action can stan...
  • PageHeader (.md): PageHeader names the page a person is on, says in one line what they do there, and holds the page's own actions and section tabs.
  • PeriodSelect (.md): PeriodSelect sets the date period a screen reports on, from a fixed preset list or a custom day range, in Lagos days.
  • SectionErrorBoundary (.md): SectionErrorBoundary keeps one section's rendering failure inside that section, with a message and a way to try again, so the rest of the...
  • SectionTabs (.md): SectionTabs switches between the sections of one page, keeps the chosen section in the URL so it can be linked, and turns into a select o...
  • Skeleton (.md): Skeleton holds the place of content that is still loading, at the size and shape that content will take, so the screen does not jump when...
  • StatusBadge (.md): StatusBadge names the state a record is in, such as Paid, Low or Resolved, in one word or two, with a tone that says how much it needs at...
  • Textarea (.md): Textarea takes free text that runs past one line, such as notes for the kitchen or a reason for cancelling, and grows with what is typed.

Rules

  • Rules (.md): every trap and rule ID, the page that answers it and the check that enforces it

Check command: node scripts/check.mjs. Machine index: llms.txt.

Button

Description

Button runs one action on the current screen when pressed, such as saving a form, recording a payment or opening a menu.

import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button", source components/ui/button.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: shadcn button (base-nova, base), on @base-ui/react/button. Traps checked: trap/button-div (Accessibility: renders a native button), trap/native-control (Examples, finding: raw copies outnumber Button), trap/role-button (ARIA), trap/link-as-button (Rules), trap/link-wraps-button (Rules), trap/button-clone (Examples, finding), trap/control-height (Variants), trap/button-icon-name (Rules, ARIA), trap/icon-optical-size (Tokens: icons 16px at default, 14px at sm, 12px at xs, NEEDS REVIEW for ink height), trap/icon-optical-align NEEDS REVIEW (not measured this session), trap/button-type (Accessibility: Base UI sets type="button"), trap/submit-repeat (States: loading disables the button while the action runs, so a second press does nothing), trap/weight-shift (States: weight never changes), trap/focus-ring-shape (Tokens: ring follows the radius), trap/hover-beats-focus (State precedence), trap/disabled-still-hovers (States: pointer-events-none), trap/disabled-drops-focus (States, finding: disabled removes focus unless focusableWhenDisabled; loading sets focusableWhenDisabled, so a pending button keeps focus), trap/loading-layout-shift and trap/loading-label-swap (States: loading adds a spinner before the label and keeps the caller's label, so the label is never swapped by Button; the spinner widens the button by its icon and gap, finding, NEEDS REVIEW for a fixed width; a caller that changes the label to "Saving…" chooses that swap itself), trap/button-label-wrap (Tokens: whitespace-nowrap), trap/tooltip-disabled-trigger n/a because Button ships no tooltip, trap/loader-small-dots (States: the loader is a 16px Loader2 spinner, not small dots), trap/touch-hover-flash and trap/hover-unguarded (States, finding: hover is not behind @media (hover: hover)), trap/touch-tap-highlight (States: active translate shows from pointer-down), trap/press-delayed (Motion), trap/motion-transition-all (Motion, finding).

Replaces

registry.json lists components/submit-button.tsx as replaced by Button (gate G-03). Old to new:

  • <SubmitButton> becomes <Button size="control">.
  • variant="primary" (SubmitButton's default) becomes variant="default".
  • variant="destructive" becomes variant="destructive-solid".
  • loading stays loading.
  • SubmitButton defaults to type="button" and so does Button; pass type="submit" on both.

Differences a migration shows:

  • Hover: SubmitButton's primary hovers to bg-primary/90. Button's default on a button element has no hover change, since only [a]:hover is set (Foundation).
  • Box: Button has border border-transparent, 1px each side, so at the same px-4 it is 2px wider than SubmitButton.
  • Motion: Button uses transition-all; SubmitButton used transition-colors.
  • Focus: Button draws a focus-visible ring; SubmitButton drew none.
  • Loading focus: SubmitButton drops focus while loading, because a native disabled button cannot hold it. Button keeps focus, through focusableWhenDisabled.
  • Destructive label: SubmitButton's was text-white; Button's is --destructive-foreground, #1A0306 in the dark theme.

const variants = ["default", "outline", "secondary", "ghost", "destructive", "link"] as const;

  );
}

Variants

variant

  • default: the one main action on a surface, filled with the green accent. Used at 4 call sites.
  • outline: a secondary action beside the main one, and the Dialog's footer Close (components/ui/dialog.tsx:112). Used at 1 call site.
  • secondary: a low-emphasis action on a tinted fill. Used at 0 call sites.
  • ghost: a quiet action in a dense row, and the Dialog and Sheet corner close (components/ui/dialog.tsx:66). Used at 3 call sites.
  • destructive: a step that deletes or voids, on a 10% destructive tint. Used at 0 call sites.
  • link: an action set inline in text. Used at 0 call sites.
  • destructive-solid: the solid destructive fill with --destructive-foreground text, for the confirm step of a void or delete, and SubmitButton's destructive. Used at 1 call site.

State precedence

  • Focus visible and hover: both show. Hover changes the fill only, so the ring stays (trap/hover-beats-focus).
  • Invalid and focus visible: invalid wins on the ring color, since aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 sits after the focus ring classes.
  • Disabled and hover: disabled wins. pointer-events-none stops hover, so nothing changes (trap/disabled-still-hovers).
  • Disabled and focus visible: disabled wins. A disabled native button cannot hold focus unless focusableWhenDisabled is set.
  • Open and pressed: open wins. active:not-aria-[haspopup] skips the 1px move on a menu trigger.
  • Pending and focus visible: both show. focusableWhenDisabled keeps focus, so the ring stays over the 50% opacity.
  • Pending and hover: pending wins. pointer-events-none stops hover.
  • Pending and disabled: pending wins on the cue, since both disable the button and only pending adds the spinner and aria-busy.
  • Pending and invalid: both show. The destructive ring and border stay under the spinner.

gen-docs writes the table from ButtonPrimitive.Props and VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants>.

  • variant: defaults to default.
  • size: defaults to default.
  • nativeButton: Base UI's flag. Set it to false whenever render swaps in a non-button element, such as a link.
  • focusableWhenDisabled: Base UI's flag. Keeps a disabled button in the tab order with aria-disabled. loading turns it on.
  • loading: team prop, defaults to false. Disables the button, keeps focus on it, sets aria-busy and shows a spinner before the label. The label is the caller's choice.
  • ButtonProps: the exported props type, ButtonPrimitive.Props plus the variant props plus loading.

Usage

When to use

  • An action that runs on this screen: save, record, export, open a menu.
  • An icon-only action in a toolbar or a corner, such as close or refresh, with an aria-label.

When not to use

  • A whole table row or a small action inside a row or drawer actions strip, the way the app draws them today. Use RowAction from DataTable instead.
  • Choosing one of 2 to 4 views or periods. Use Segmented instead.
  • Confirming a destructive step. Use ConfirmDialog instead, with Button inside it.

Rules

  • rule/button-link-render: When the action navigates to another route, render one element with render={<Link href="/sales/new" />} and nativeButton={false} instead of wrapping a Button in a Link or a Link in a Button, because nested link and button give two tab stops and two roles for one action and are invalid HTML. Evidence: principle platform: an a may not contain interactive content and a button may not contain an a (HTML content model), and Base UI's render merges Button's props onto the one element. Check: review.
  • Don't: <Link href="/sales/new"><Button>Record sale</Button></Link>
  • Do: <Button nativeButton={false} render={<Link href="/sales/new" />}>Record sale</Button>
  • rule/button-icon-name: When size is icon, icon-xs, icon-sm or icon-lg, pass an aria-label naming the action and mark the icon aria-hidden instead of leaving the glyph as the only content, because the button then has no accessible name and a screen reader says only "button". Evidence: principle wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value, an icon-only control needs a text name; app 3/3 icon-only close controls in the kit and ui folder carry a name, components/app/entity-drawer.tsx:52, components/ui/dialog.tsx:66, components/ui/sheet.tsx:66. Check: review, and an a11y scan of the page.
  • Don't: <Button size="icon" variant="ghost"><X /></Button>
  • Do: <Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Close"><X aria-hidden /></Button>

Content

  • rule/button-label-verb-first: When a Button holds text, write it in sentence case starting with a verb and naming the object, such as "Record payment", instead of Title Case or a bare noun such as "Payment", because the label is the action's accessible name and the app's action labels already read this way. Evidence: app 3/3 text actions in the customer drawer header start with a verb in sentence case, "Record sale", "Record payment", "Log interaction", app/(app)/customers/customer-detail-panel.tsx:115. Check: review.
  • Don't: <Button>Record Payment</Button>
  • Do: <Button>Record payment</Button>

Anti-slop

  • rule/button-destructive-variant: When the action deletes, voids or cancels, use variant="destructive" instead of palette classes such as className="bg-red-600 text-white", because palette classes skip the --destructive token and its dark-mode value. Evidence: app 2/2 destructive submits in drawers name a destructive variant, app/(app)/kitchen/job-panel.tsx:163, app/(app)/sales/sale-detail-panel.tsx:135. Check: review, plus rg -n "bg-red-" app components lib.
  • Don't: <Button className="bg-red-600 text-white">Void sale</Button>
  • Do: <Button variant="destructive">Void sale</Button>

Limits

Not applicable: Button has no call sites on a screen, so no label length or count was measured on a real route this session. whitespace-nowrap keeps one line, and the wrap break at 390px is NOT SUPPLIED until a probe runs.

Accessibility

Rests on Base UI's Button, which renders a native button with type="button" by default (Base UI useButton, in the installed @base-ui/react package), so a Button inside a form does not submit unless type="submit" is passed (trap/button-type).

Checkbox

Description

Checkbox lets someone turn one option on or off, or pick several options from a list, where each choice stands on its own.

import { Checkbox } from "@/components/ui/checkbox", source components/ui/checkbox.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: shadcn checkbox (base-nova, base) on @base-ui/react/checkbox. Traps checked: trap/color-only-status (States: a check mark or a dash shows the value, not the fill alone), trap/reduced-motion-ignored n/a because only transition-colors runs, trap/motion-layout-property (Motion: colours only), trap/live-region-double n/a because Checkbox announces only its own state, trap/decor-pointer n/a because Checkbox draws no decoration over a control.

Foundation

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
base-ui Checkbox.Root and Checkbox.Indicator: a span with role="checkbox", aria-checked (true, false or mixed), a hidden native input for forms, and the data-checked, data-unchecked, data-indeterminate and data-disabled attributesA MinusIcon for the indeterminate state beside the CheckIcon, chosen by group-data-indeterminate, since base-ui shows the indicator for both states
shadcn base-nova classes: size-4 box, border-input, data-checked:bg-primary, focus ring and aria-invalid stylesThe radius is rounded-sm from the scale instead of an arbitrary 4px value, and the icon size is set on each icon (size-3.5)

The app still draws 16 raw native checkboxes instead (rg -n 'type="checkbox"' app components lib --glob '*.tsx'), such as components/app/data-table.tsx:159, app/(app)/sales/sales-filter-bar.tsx:87 and app/(app)/kitchen/settings.tsx:130. Moving them onto Checkbox is migration work, not part of this spec.

State precedence

  • Indeterminate and checked: indeterminate wins. The dash shows and aria-checked is mixed.
  • Disabled and any other state: both show. The value stays visible at 50% opacity.
  • Invalid and checked: both show. The red ring sits round the filled box.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
A change of value, focus or invalid stateinputtransition-colors, Tailwind's 150ms default, no named presetbackground-color, border-color, colorNot handled, a 150ms colour fade only (NEEDS REVIEW)

Props

No props of its own.

Also accepts: @base-ui/react props (16); native element attributes from React's types.

gen-docs writes the table from CheckboxPrimitive.Root.Props. Checkbox adds no props of its own.

  • checked: the controlled value. Pair it with onCheckedChange.

The base-ui indeterminate prop shows the dash and sets aria-checked="mixed".

Usage

When to use

  • An option that someone turns on or off and that takes effect when the form is saved, such as "Include running costs".
  • A list where several options can be picked at once, such as filter options or table rows.

When not to use

  • A setting that takes effect the moment it changes. Use Switch instead.
  • One choice out of a list. Use Select instead.

Rules

  • Not applicable: Checkbox has 1 call site, too few for any rule to rest on app evidence yet. The raw-checkbox migration (G-04) brings the first ones.

Content

  • Not applicable: Checkbox renders no text. The label is the caller's Label, in sentence case, such as "Only show overdue jobs".

Anti-slop

  • Not applicable: no rule has app evidence yet. The 16 raw native checkboxes are counted under Examples.

Limits

  • Not applicable: no list length limit was measured this session.

Accessibility

Rests on base-ui Checkbox: a span with role="checkbox" that takes focus, plus a hidden native input that carries the value into a form. It has no visible name of its own, so the caller joins a Label with id and htmlFor, or passes aria-label.

DataTable

Description

DataTable lists records of one kind so someone can scan them, sort by a column, page through them and open one.

import { DataTable, RowAction, type Column } from "@/components/app", source components/app/data-table.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled on the native table element, with Skeleton from components/ui/skeleton.tsx, PaginationControls from components/ui/pagination-controls.tsx and FilterSelect from components/filter-select.tsx. Traps checked: trap/table-divs (Accessibility), trap/list-dead-gap (Rules, rule/data-table-row-padding), trap/narrow-hidden-nav (Rules, rule/data-table-mobile-slots), trap/numbers-shift (Tokens and Rules, rule/data-table-right-figures), trap/color-only-status (Anti-slop, rule/data-table-status-cell), trap/empty-value (finding: cells are caller-rendered and no shared empty-value component exists, so blanks, dashes and "None" all occur; proposed gate in the run report), trap/motion-blocks-input (Motion: rows and actions only change colour, nothing enters), trap/loading-layout-shift (States: skeleton rows keep the header and column widths), trap/loading-label-swap n/a because RowAction has no pending state, trap/submit-repeat (finding: a RowAction that runs a request, such as Approve at app/(app)/inventory/requests-tab.tsx:116, has no pending block), trap/disabled-drops-focus n/a because RowAction has no disabled state, trap/button-type (RowAction and the sort and title buttons set type="button"), trap/button-div n/a because every control is a button, a or Link, trap/link-as-button (RowAction renders Link or a for href and button for onClick), trap/button-label-wrap (RowAction sets whitespace-nowrap), trap/button-icon-name (Accessibility: icons are aria-hidden and labels are text), trap/control-height (RowAction is h-8, 32px), trap/icon-optical-size and trap/icon-optical-align NEEDS REVIEW because no optical measurement ran this session, trap/press-delayed (Motion: colour only, Tailwind default duration).

Example: Customers with credit, sortable, rows open a drawer, one WhatsApp action per row (docs/system/examples/data-table/default.tsx)

import { DataTable, RowAction, type Column } from "@/components/app";

type Credit = { id: string; customer: string; owed: number; days: number };

const rows: Credit[] = [
  { id: "c1", customer: "Mama Put Kitchen", owed: 48500, days: 12 },
  { id: "c2", customer: "Lagos Grill House", owed: 12000, days: 3 },
  { id: "c3", customer: "Ada Foods", owed: 90250, days: 41 },
];

const columns: Column<Credit>[] = [
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", cell: (r) => r.customer, sortValue: (r) => r.customer, mobile: "title" },
  { id: "days", header: "Days open", cell: (r) => r.days, sortValue: (r) => r.days, align: "right", mobile: "subtitle" },
  { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => `₦${r.owed.toLocaleString()}`, sortValue: (r) => r.owed, align: "right", mobile: "value" },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <DataTable
      label="Customers with credit"
      columns={columns}
      rows={rows}
      getRowId={(r) => r.id}
      onRowClick={() => {}}
      defaultSort={{ id: "days", dir: "desc" }}
      rowActions={(r) => (
        <RowAction href="https://wa.me/2348000000000" external ariaLabel={`WhatsApp ${r.customer}`}>WhatsApp</RowAction>
      )}
    />
  );
}

tone

RowAction's only axis. DataTable itself has no variant prop: its modes come from which callbacks a call site passes (onRowClick, rowActions, bulkActions, pagination), counted under Examples.

  • default: a secondary row action, such as WhatsApp, View, Edit or Transfer. Used at 19 RowAction call sites.
  • primary: the one next step that moves the record forward, such as Record payment, Approve or Resolve. Used at 9 RowAction call sites with a literal, plus 1 that picks the tone from the record (app/(app)/engagement/compensation-table.tsx:68).

Example: First load: the header stays and skeleton rows hold the space, never the empty slot (docs/system/examples/data-table/loading.tsx)

import { DataTable, type Column } from "@/components/app";
import { EmptyState } from "@/components/app/empty-state";

type Credit = { id: string; customer: string; owed: number; days: number };

const rows: Credit[] = [
  { id: "c1", customer: "Mama Put Kitchen", owed: 48500, days: 12 },
  { id: "c2", customer: "Lagos Grill House", owed: 12000, days: 3 },
  { id: "c3", customer: "Ada Foods", owed: 90250, days: 41 },
];

const columns: Column<Credit>[] = [
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", cell: (r) => r.customer, sortValue: (r) => r.customer, mobile: "title" },
  { id: "days", header: "Days open", cell: (r) => r.days, sortValue: (r) => r.days, align: "right", mobile: "subtitle" },
  { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => `₦${r.owed.toLocaleString()}`, sortValue: (r) => r.owed, align: "right", mobile: "value" },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <DataTable
      label="Customers with credit"
      columns={columns}
      rows={undefined}
      loading
      getRowId={(r) => r.id}
      empty={<EmptyState size="compact" title="No customers owe credit" description="Credit sales appear here once recorded." />}
    />
  );
}

Example: Server pages: rows are one page, the footer shows the range and page buttons (docs/system/examples/data-table/paged.tsx)

import { DataTable, type Column } from "@/components/app";

type Credit = { id: string; customer: string; owed: number; days: number };

const rows: Credit[] = [
  { id: "c1", customer: "Mama Put Kitchen", owed: 48500, days: 12 },
  { id: "c2", customer: "Lagos Grill House", owed: 12000, days: 3 },
  { id: "c3", customer: "Ada Foods", owed: 90250, days: 41 },
];

const columns: Column<Credit>[] = [
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", cell: (r) => r.customer, sortValue: (r) => r.customer, mobile: "title" },
  { id: "days", header: "Days open", cell: (r) => r.days, sortValue: (r) => r.days, align: "right", mobile: "subtitle" },
  { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => `₦${r.owed.toLocaleString()}`, sortValue: (r) => r.owed, align: "right", mobile: "value" },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <DataTable
      label="Customers with credit"
      columns={columns}
      rows={rows}
      getRowId={(r) => r.id}
      manualSort
      pagination={{ page: 2, totalPages: 5, onPageChange: () => {}, pageSize: 25, onPageSizeChange: () => {}, total: 110 }}
    />
  );
}

State precedence

  • Loading and empty: loading wins. isEmpty needs loading false, so the empty slot never shows during the first fetch.
  • Loading and populated: populated wins. With rows in hand the skeleton never replaces them, so a refetch shows the old rows with no cue.
  • Loading and paged: loading wins. The footer hides while the skeleton shows.
  • Empty and paged: empty wins. The footer hides, so no "0 to 0" range shows.
  • Sorted and loading: both show. The header keeps its arrow over the skeleton rows.
  • Selected and row hover: both show. The checkbox stays ticked; while the pointer is over the row the hover background shows instead of the selected tint.
  • Selected and paged: both show. Selection is kept by row id across client pages, and the bar counts every selected row in the sorted list.
  • Phone layout and any other state: both show. The phone list draws the same loading, empty and selected states with 4 skeleton cards.

gen-docs writes the tables for DataTable, RowAction and TableFooter from the types.

  • label names the scroll region and the phone list for screen readers, and is the storage key for the remembered page size unless pageSizeKey is set.
  • rows set to undefined with loading true is how 12 call sites write the first load. An empty array with loading false is the empty state.
  • empty is shown only after loading ends with no rows. 22 of the 28 counted call sites that pass it pass EmptyState with size="compact", and 6 pass a plain paragraph.
  • rowActions returns the row's buttons: RowAction for labelled actions and OverflowMenu for the rest.
  • pagination switches to server pages: rows is one page and the table stops slicing.
  • tone on RowAction is default or primary.

Usage

When to use

  • A screen lists records of one kind, such as customers, sales, stock or tills, that someone scans, sorts or opens
  • A dashboard widget shows the top 5 or 10 records of a kind with a fixed page size

When not to use

  • A single number or a row of headline figures. Use KpiStrip instead
  • A short list of a record's own history inside a drawer, such as price changes. Use EntityDrawer instead, with its own list
  • Nothing to list yet and the whole section is empty. Use EmptyState instead, at size="default"

Rules

  • rule/data-table-loading-prop: When the rows come from a query, pass loading={isLoading} and rows={data} to DataTable instead of wrapping it in a spinner or a hand-made Skeleton, because the table keeps its header, draws 6 skeleton rows and holds back the empty slot until the fetch ends (components/app/data-table.tsx:129). Evidence: app 24/24 call sites with fetched rows pass loading, counted in the props of each <DataTable tag, and the 8 without it render rows handed down by a parent that shows its own loading state, such as the Analytics page. Check: review.
  • Don't: {isLoading ? <Spinner /> : <DataTable label="Sales" columns={columns} rows={data} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />}
  • Do: <DataTable label="Sales" columns={columns} rows={data} loading={isLoading} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • rule/data-table-reset-page: When the rows are filtered on the client, pass the active filters as resetPageKey instead of remounting the table with a key, because resetPageKey returns to page 1 and keeps the sort and selection, while a remount drops both. Evidence: app 12/14 client-filtered call sites pass resetPageKey, with strays app/(app)/inventory/movements-tab.tsx:134 and app/(app)/inventory/stock-tab.tsx:195 use key and are strays. Check: review.
  • Don't: <DataTable key={filterKey} label="Stock movements" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • Do: <DataTable resetPageKey={filterKey} label="Stock movements" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • rule/data-table-row-padding: When a row needs more room or a divider, add padding inside the cells through className or rowClassName instead of a margin between rows, because the rows share divide-y borders and touch, so every pixel between two rows belongs to one of them and opens it. Evidence: principle heuristic: Fitts's law, the hit areas of adjacent rows touch with no dead gap (trap/list-dead-gap); app 32/32 call sites leave the row spacing to the component, and the 5 that pass rowClassName only mute, fade or tint the row. Check: review.
  • Don't: <DataTable rowClassName={() => "mb-2"} label="Tills" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • Do: <DataTable label="Tills" columns={[{ id: "name", header: "Till", cell: (r) => r.name, className: "py-4" }]} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • rule/data-table-mobile-slots: When a column must stay visible on phones, give it a mobile slot (title, subtitle, value or meta) instead of leaving it out, because a column with no mobile slot is not drawn below 768px and nothing on screen says it is missing. Evidence: principle heuristic: visibility of system status, a hidden column leaves no cue (trap/narrow-hidden-nav), and 36 columns in 31 files already set mobile: 'title' (grep -rln "mobile: 'title'" app components lib). Check: review.
  • Don't: { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => money(r.owed), align: "right" }
  • Do: { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => money(r.owed), align: "right", mobile: "value" }
  • rule/data-table-right-figures: When a column holds amounts, counts or percentages, set align: "right" on it instead of left-aligning figures, because right-aligned cells get tabular-nums (components/app/data-table.tsx:202), so digits line up down the column and do not jitter on re-sort. Evidence: principle platform: tabular figures in Geist, the visual rule "Figures use tabular-nums" in app/globals.css:10. Check: review.
  • Don't: { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => money(r.owed) }
  • Do: { id: "owed", header: "Owed", cell: (r) => money(r.owed), align: "right", mobile: "value" }
  • rule/data-table-whatsapp-contact: When a row action contacts a customer, render RowAction with a WhatsApp href, external and the label "WhatsApp" instead of a tel: link labelled "Call", because customers are reached by WhatsApp only in this product. Evidence: app 2/2 customer-contact row actions use WhatsApp, app/(app)/_dashboard/needs-attention.tsx:56 and app/(app)/credits/page.tsx:190, and the one tel: RowAction, app/(app)/suppliers/supplier-drawer.tsx:71, calls a supplier and is in the run report. Check: review.
  • Don't: <RowAction href={tel:${r.phone}}>Call</RowAction>
  • Do: <RowAction href={whatsAppHref(r.phone)} external ariaLabel={WhatsApp ${r.customerName}}>WhatsApp</RowAction>

Content

  • rule/data-table-label-noun: When setting label, write what the rows are as a sentence-case plural noun phrase, such as "Customers with credit" or "Stock movements", instead of a verb or "Table", because label is the accessible name of the scroll region and the phone list, and the key of the remembered page size. Evidence: app 32/32 call sites pass a noun phrase in sentence case, read from the label= values in the props of each <DataTable tag. Check: review.
  • Don't: <DataTable label="Table" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • Do: <DataTable label="Customers with credit" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • rule/data-table-action-verb: When a RowAction has a visible label, write a sentence-case verb or verb phrase of 1 to 3 words, such as "Record payment", "Approve" or "View tills", instead of an icon alone, because the label is the button's only name unless ariaLabel is set. Evidence: app 28/29 RowAction tags carry a literal text label of 1 to 3 words and the 29th renders next.label from data, from each <RowAction tag in app, components and lib. Check: review.
  • Don't: <RowAction onClick={pay}><Wallet aria-hidden /></RowAction>
  • Do: <RowAction tone="primary" onClick={pay}><Wallet aria-hidden /> Record payment</RowAction>

Anti-slop

  • rule/data-table-empty-compact: When the table can end up with no rows, pass empty={<EmptyState size="compact" title={...} description={...} />} instead of leaving the fallback "Nothing to show.", because the fallback names neither the filter behind the empty result nor the way out. Evidence: app 22/32 call sites pass empty with a compact EmptyState, and the 3 typed tables at app/(app)/_dashboard/needs-attention.tsx:48 do too, with 10 strays: 4 pass nothing (app/(app)/analytics/inventory-tab.tsx:189, app/(app)/analytics/products-tab.tsx:150, app/(app)/analytics/suppliers-tab.tsx:238, app/(app)/suppliers/supplier-performance-tab.tsx:180) and 6 pass a plain paragraph (app/(app)/analytics/credit-tab.tsx:127, app/(app)/analytics/customers-tab.tsx:152, app/(app)/analytics/products-tab.tsx:132, app/(app)/analytics/sales-tab.tsx:217, components/kitchen-analytics-tab.tsx:124, components/live-pos-panel.tsx:55). Check: review.
  • Don't: <DataTable label="Suppliers" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  • Do: <DataTable label="Suppliers" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} empty={<EmptyState size="compact" title="No suppliers match" description="Clear the filters to see every supplier." />} />
  • rule/data-table-status-cell: When a column shows a record's state, such as Paid, Overdue or Low, render StatusBadge in the cell instead of coloured text, because the badge carries the state word and its tone from one table, and colour alone does not tell the state. Evidence: principle wcag: 1.4.1 Use of colour, the badge text carries the state. Check: review.
  • Don't: { id: "status", header: "Status", cell: (r) => <span className="text-destructive">{r.status}</span> }
  • Do: { id: "status", header: "Status", cell: (r) => <StatusBadge domain="payment" status={r.status} />, mobile: "meta" }

Limits

  • Not applicable: no break was measured this session. The JSDoc cap of 2 labelled row buttons plus an OverflowMenu (components/app/data-table.tsx:37) has no measurement behind it, so it goes to the run report as a proposed gate with the app's current maximum, 2, as its default.

Accessibility

Rests on the native table element with th scope="col" and aria-sort, a native ul for phone cards, and native button, a and checkbox input elements. Contrast: NEEDS REVIEW, not measured this session.

Related

  • EmptyState: what the table shows in its empty slot, at size="compact".
  • StatusBadge: the state of a record inside a cell.
  • OverflowMenu: row actions past the labelled ones, destructive last.
  • EntityDrawer: what onRowClick opens.
  • KpiStrip: the headline figures above a table.
  • Button: standalone actions above or beside the table, not inside rows (RowAction there).

EmptyState

Description

EmptyState tells someone why a list, panel or section has nothing in it and what would fill it.

import { EmptyState } from "@/components/app", source components/app/empty-state.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/illustration-announced (ARIA: the icon slot is aria-hidden), trap/decor-pointer n/a because the icon and text take no pointer events of their own and only the caller's action is interactive, trap/surface-double-edge (Rules, rule/empty-state-compact-inside: EmptyState draws no border or fill, so it adds no edge inside a DataTable or card), trap/surface-matches-parent n/a because it has no surface, trap/loading-layout-shift and trap/loading-label-swap n/a because EmptyState has no loading state and DataTable never shows it during a load, trap/toast-errors, trap/toast-timer, trap/live-region-double n/a because it is not a toast and has no live region (finding: nothing is announced when filters empty a list), trap/numbers-shift n/a because it shows no figures, trap/color-only-status n/a because it is neutral and its state is the title text, trap/icon-optical-size and trap/icon-optical-align NEEDS REVIEW because no optical measurement ran this session, trap/loader-small-dots, trap/demo-on-timers, trap/reduced-motion-ignored, trap/loop-offscreen, trap/motion-restart, trap/motion-layout-property, trap/motion-blocks-input n/a because it has no motion, trap/viewport-height, trap/safe-area, trap/scroll-chain, trap/gesture-drag, trap/gesture-axes, trap/overflow-scrollbar n/a because it never sizes to the viewport or scrolls.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled. The component is 10 lines of flex layout in components/app/empty-state.tsx with no library underneath.

States

EmptyState renders the same parts in every case. Its states are the reasons a caller shows it, told by the title and description.

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
FilteredFilters or a search leave no rowsClear the filters from the action, or change themTitle "No {records} match" or "No {records} to show", description "Nothing matches these filters." or the filter names, action "Clear filters"screenshot
First runNothing of this kind recorded yetTake the first step from the action when the person may, such as "Add ingredient"Title "No {records} yet", description saying what makes rows appearscreenshot
Nothing dueA queue the person works through is clear, such as overdue creditRead it and move onTitle such as "Nothing owed", "Stock is healthy" or "Nothing to review"screenshot
No accessThe person lacks the permission for the sectionRead who can grant itTitle "No access" or "No access to {section}", description naming the permissionby hand
Needs the APIThe app runs without its API, so the section has no data sourceRead itTitle "{Section} needs the API"by hand
Load failedThe caller's query failedRead what to try; no retry action exists todayTitle "Couldn’t load {thing}" or "Could not load {thing}", description "Check your connection and try again."by hand

State precedence

Not applicable: each call site passes one title and description for one reason, and the caller picks the reason before rendering, as in app/(app)/engagement/churn.tsx:174 where load failed and filtered are separate branches.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
titlestring
action?ReactNode"Clear filters" or the first action, e.g.
className?string
description?ReactNodeSay why it's empty: name the active filters or what would make rows appear.
icon?ReactNode
size?"default" | "compact""default"compact = inside a table or panel; default = a whole section.

gen-docs writes the table from the types.

  • title is the only required prop and the only one every call site passes.
  • description takes a node so a caller can name the active filters inline.
  • icon takes a lucide icon, sized to 24px and muted by the component.
  • action takes the caller's own control. 22 call sites pass one.
  • size is default or compact.

Usage

When to use

  • A list, table or panel loaded and has nothing to show, and the person needs to know why
  • A whole section cannot show data because the person lacks access or the API is not connected

When not to use

  • A list is still loading. Use DataTable instead, with loading, which shows skeleton rows and holds the empty slot back
  • A single field or cell has no value. Use StatusBadge instead when the blank is a state such as "Unpaid", else leave it to the cell
  • A section crashed while rendering. Use SectionErrorBoundary instead

Rules

  • rule/empty-state-compact-inside: When EmptyState sits inside a DataTable empty slot, a drawer panel or a card, set size="compact" instead of the default, because the default's 56px of space above and below suits a whole section and pushes a panel's other content down. Evidence: app 51/55 call sites pass size="compact", and the 4 default ones fill a whole Analytics section or tab. Check: review.
  • Don't: <DataTable label="Tills" columns={columns} rows={[]} getRowId={(r) => r.id} empty={<EmptyState title="No tills" />} />
  • Do: <DataTable label="Tills" columns={columns} rows={[]} getRowId={(r) => r.id} empty={<EmptyState size="compact" title="No tills" description="Register a till to start selling from a device at this location." />} />
  • rule/empty-state-filtered-clear: When filters or a search caused the empty result, pass an action labelled "Clear filters" that clears them, instead of no action, because the filters often sit above the fold on a phone and the empty slot is where the person is looking. Evidence: app 12/22 filtered empty states pass a "Clear filters" action, the 10 strays listed in docs/system/rule-tests/empty-state.tsv. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No suppliers match" description="Nothing matches these filters." />
  • Do: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No suppliers match" description="Nothing matches these filters." action={<button type="button" onClick={clearAll} className="text-sm font-medium text-primary hover:underline">Clear filters</button>} />
  • rule/empty-state-action-link: When passing an action, render a text button with text-sm font-medium text-primary hover:underline instead of a filled primary Button, because the screen's one filled primary action lives in its page header and a second filled green button competes with it. Evidence: app 16/22 actions use the text button classes, read at each call site listed in the props of each <EmptyState tag; principle heuristic: one primary action per screen, the one-green-accent rule in app/globals.css:11. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EmptyState title="No recipes yet" action={<Button>New recipe</Button>} />
  • Do: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No recipes yet" action={<button type="button" onClick={add} className="text-sm font-medium text-primary hover:underline">New recipe</button>} />

Content

  • rule/empty-state-title-no: When writing title, start with "No {records}" and end on "yet", "match" or "to show" for first-run, filtered and plain empty cases, in sentence case with no full stop, instead of "Empty" or "No data", because the title is the one line every call site shows and it names what is missing. Evidence: app 47/53 titles start with "No" or "Nothing", from the props of each <EmptyState tag. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No data." />
  • Do: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No suppliers match" />
  • rule/empty-state-description-why: When writing description, say in 1 or 2 full sentences why it is empty or what makes rows appear, such as "Purchases recorded against this supplier show up here.", ending with a full stop, instead of repeating the title, because the title already says what is missing and the description is the only place for the reason. Evidence: app 54/55 call sites pass a description, the stray app/(app)/inventory/product-drawer-panels.tsx:215 passes the title only. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No purchases yet" description="There are no purchases." />
  • Do: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No purchases yet" description="Purchases recorded against this supplier show up here." />

Anti-slop

  • rule/empty-state-icon-only: When adding art, pass one lucide icon through icon instead of an illustration, an emoji or a tinted circle behind the icon, because the component draws the icon at 24px in --muted-foreground and the visual rules keep the brand palette out of state. Evidence: app 32/55 call sites pass a lucide icon and 0 pass an image or emoji, from the props of each <EmptyState tag. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EmptyState title="No sales yet" icon={<div className="rounded-full bg-primary/10 p-3"><img src="/empty.svg" alt="" /></div>} />
  • Do: <EmptyState size="compact" title="No sales yet" icon={<Receipt />} description="Retail sales of this product appear here." />
  • rule/empty-state-whatsapp-contact: When an empty state's action reaches a customer, set its href to whatsAppHref(phone) instead of a tel: call link, because customers are contacted by WhatsApp only in this product. Evidence: app 2/2 customer-contact actions in the row kit use WhatsApp, app/(app)/_dashboard/needs-attention.tsx:56 and app/(app)/credits/page.tsx:190, and 0 of 22 EmptyState actions place a call. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EmptyState size="compact" title="Nothing owed" action={<a href={tel:${phone}}>Call customer</a>} />
  • Do: <EmptyState size="compact" title="Nothing owed" action={<a href={whatsAppHref(phone)} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="text-sm font-medium text-primary hover:underline">WhatsApp</a>} />

Limits

  • Not applicable: no break was measured this session. The description wraps inside max-w-sm (384px), and the longest real description, at app/(app)/kitchen/ingredients.tsx:137, was not measured at 390px.

Accessibility

Rests on plain div and p elements. The title is a paragraph, not a heading, and the icon is aria-hidden. Contrast: NEEDS REVIEW, not measured this session.

KeyWhere focus isEffectFocus afterChecked by

ARIA

Related

  • DataTable: shows EmptyState in its empty slot after loading ends with no rows.
  • SectionErrorBoundary: a section that crashed, rather than one with no data.
  • StatusBadge: a single record's state, not a whole empty list.

EntityDrawer

Description

EntityDrawer shows one record, such as a customer, sale, product or supplier, beside the list it was opened from, with that record's identity, key figures, actions and sections.

import { EntityDrawer } from "@/components/app", source components/app/entity-drawer.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled, on the team's ModalDialog (components/ui/modal-dialog.tsx, a native <dialog open>). Traps checked: trap/overlay-title (ARIA), trap/overlay-focus-return (Keyboard, finding when the opener is gone), trap/overlay-conditional-render (States, accepted: callers mount it, no exit motion exists to break), trap/escape-nested (Keyboard), trap/overlay-pending-dismiss (States, Rules), trap/overlay-destructive (Rules: destructive actions sit in overflow and confirm through their own step), trap/overlay-no-max-height (States: full-height panel, body scrolls), trap/native-control (Foundation, finding: the close control is a raw <button>), trap/button-icon-name (ARIA), trap/color-only-status (States, finding on stat tones), trap/touch-autofocus (Keyboard, finding), trap/scroll-chain (finding: no page scroll lock), trap/viewport-height n/a because the panel is h-full of a fixed inset-0 dialog and uses no vh, trap/open-trigger-unfocused n/a because the drawer is modal and covers its opener, trap/exit-eats-input, trap/motion-origin, trap/motion-restart, trap/motion-blocks-input and trap/reduced-motion-ignored n/a because the drawer has no motion of its own (the loading bars are Skeleton's, answered there), trap/gesture-drag, trap/gesture-axes and trap/motion-input-lag n/a because it has no drag or swipe.

Foundation

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
ModalDialog: native <dialog open> with aria-modal, Escape handled by the topmost open dialog only, backdrop click to close, focus moved in on open and back to the opener on close, dismissiblealign="end" side sheet at sm:max-w-xl (md) or sm:max-w-3xl (lg), full height, left border and shadow-xl
labelledBy naming the dialog from a visible headingA sticky header: h2 title wired to labelledBy through useId, status slot, muted subtitle, a close button, then an actions row with overflow pushed to the end
Nothing for figures or sectionsA stats grid (dl, 2 columns on phones, 3 or 4 from sm), tabs through SectionTabs (inline up to 3 visible tabs on phones, a select past that), and a loading body of three Skeleton bars in a status region
Not applicable: the close controlThe close control is a raw <button> with an X icon (components/app/entity-drawer.tsx:52), not the system Button, so it misses Button's focus ring (trap/native-control, finding)

Example: Customer drawer at the default md width, with a WhatsApp action, three stats and three tabs (docs/system/examples/entity-drawer/default.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { MessageCircle, ShoppingCart } from 'lucide-react';
import { EntityDrawer } from '@/components/app';
import { RowAction } from '@/components/app/data-table';
import { StatusBadge } from '@/components/app/status-badge';

type Tab = 'overview' | 'purchases' | 'credit';

export default function EntityDrawerDefault() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState<Tab>('overview');
  return (
    <EntityDrawer
      onClose={() => {}}
      title="Mama Put Kitchen"
      subtitle="0803 123 4567 · Restaurant · Ikeja"
      status={<StatusBadge tone="good">Active</StatusBadge>}
      actions={
        <>
          <RowAction href="https://wa.me/2348031234567" external><MessageCircle aria-hidden /> WhatsApp</RowAction>
          <RowAction href="/sales/new"><ShoppingCart aria-hidden /> Record sale</RowAction>
        </>
      }
      stats={[
        { label: 'Lifetime spend', value: '₦1,240,000' },
        { label: 'Outstanding', value: '₦45,000', tone: 'warning' },
        { label: 'Last purchase', value: '18 Nov 26' },
      ]}
      tabs={{
        items: [
          { id: 'overview', label: 'Overview' },
          { id: 'purchases', label: 'Purchases', count: 24 },
          { id: 'credit', label: 'Credit' },
        ],
        value: tab,
        onChange: setTab,
      }}
    >
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Overview of this customer.</p>
    </EntityDrawer>
  );
}

Variants

width

  • md: the default. A record read as fields and short lists, such as a customer, supplier or enquiry. Used at 11 call sites by omission, plus audit-drawer.tsx for a single entry.
  • lg: a record whose main tab holds a multi-column table, such as a sale's line items or a product's batches. Used at 5 call sites, plus audit-drawer.tsx for bulk uploads.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
OpenThe caller mounts it, usually from a list row clickRead, run an action, switch tabs, close with the close button, Escape or a backdrop clickA full-height panel at the right edge with the record's title as an h2, aria-modal="true"by hand

Example: Drawer whose record is still loading, three skeleton bars in a status region (docs/system/examples/entity-drawer/loading.tsx)

import { EntityDrawer } from '@/components/app';

export default function EntityDrawerLoading() {
  return (
    <EntityDrawer onClose={() => {}} title="Mama Put Kitchen" loading>
      <p className="text-sm">Not shown while loading.</p>
    </EntityDrawer>
  );

Example: Enquiry drawer holding an unsaved note, so Escape and a backdrop click do nothing (docs/system/examples/entity-drawer/locked.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { EntityDrawer } from '@/components/app';
import { StatusBadge } from '@/components/app/status-badge';

export default function EntityDrawerLocked() {
  const saved = '';
  const [note, setNote] = useState('Called back, wants a bulk price');
  return (
    <EntityDrawer
      onClose={() => {}}
      dismissible={note === saved}
      title="Bulk order for December"
      subtitle="Enquiry from Mama Put Kitchen"
      status={<StatusBadge domain="work" status="Open" />}
    >
      <label className="block text-sm font-medium" htmlFor="resolution">Resolution note</label>
      <textarea id="resolution" className="mt-1 w-full rounded-md border p-2 text-sm" value={note} onChange={(e) => setNote(e.target.value)} />
    </EntityDrawer>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Loading and locked: both show. The skeleton fills the body and Escape still does nothing.
  • Loading and stats or tabs: both show. Stats and tabs render above the skeleton, so a caller that passes stats before the record loads shows them with placeholder values such as "…".
  • Locked and a close button press: the close button wins. onClose runs and unsaved text is lost unless the caller's onClose guards it (finding).
  • Locked and a nested ModalDialog such as ConfirmDialog: the nested dialog wins Escape, because only the topmost open ModalDialog handles it.
  • Stat in state and long title: both show.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion. The drawer appears and leaves at once. The loading bars pulse through Skeleton, whose spec covers that motion.

gen-docs writes the table from EntityDrawerProps in components/app/entity-drawer.tsx.

  • dismissible: defaults to true. Callers compute it from their own dirty state, such as dismissible={!dirty}.
  • loading: replaces the children with skeleton bars. No call site passes it today.
  • actions: the JSDoc names "Call" as an example action. Customers are contacted by WhatsApp only, so the example is wrong for customer drawers (finding).

Usage

When to use

  • Someone opens one record from a list or table and needs its figures, actions and history without leaving the list.
  • A record has two or more sections that each hold a list, such as Purchases and Credit for a customer.

When not to use

  • The person is creating or editing a record through a form with a submit. Use FormSheet instead.
  • The person confirms one destructive step, such as voiding a sale. Use ConfirmDialog instead.

Rules

  • rule/entity-drawer-dismissible-dirty: When the drawer holds typed text that is not saved yet, pass dismissible computed from that state, such as dismissible={!dirty}, instead of the default true, because an Escape or a backdrop click would close the drawer and drop the text. Evidence: app 4/5 drawers with in-drawer text entry pass it, app/(app)/engagement/enquiry-drawer.tsx:40, app/(app)/engagement/feedback-drawer.tsx:67, app/(app)/suppliers/supplier-drawer.tsx:65, app/(app)/kitchen/job-panel.tsx:137, stray app/(app)/sales/sale-detail-panel.tsx:87 (edit mode with no dismissible). Check: review.
  • Don't: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title={enquiry.subject}><textarea value={note} onChange={(e) => setNote(e.target.value)} /></EntityDrawer>
  • Do: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} dismissible={note === saved} title={enquiry.subject}><textarea value={note} onChange={(e) => setNote(e.target.value)} /></EntityDrawer>
  • rule/entity-drawer-destructive-overflow: When a drawer action deletes, voids, cancels or deactivates the record, put it in overflow as an OverflowMenu item with destructive: true instead of in actions, because the actions row holds the frequent task and one slip there would destroy the record. Evidence: app 4/4 drawers with a destructive action put it in the overflow menu, app/(app)/kitchen/job-panel.tsx:110, app/(app)/suppliers/supplier-drawer.tsx:82, app/(app)/sales/sale-detail-panel.tsx:108, found by rg -n "destructive: true" over the 17 call-site files. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="Sale S-10482" actions={<RowAction onClick={voidSale}>Void sale</RowAction>}>{body}</EntityDrawer>
  • Do: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="Sale S-10482" overflow={<OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Void sale', destructive: true, onSelect: askToVoid }]} />}>{body}</EntityDrawer>

Content

  • rule/entity-drawer-loading-title: When the record has not loaded, the title reads "Loading {object}…", and when it failed it reads "{Object} unavailable", instead of an empty title or the record id, because the title is the dialog's accessible name and is all a screen reader hears on open. Evidence: app 3/3 loading shells, app/(app)/kitchen/job-form.tsx:99, app/(app)/kitchen/recipes.tsx:110, app/(app)/kitchen/job-panel.tsx:41. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="">{spinner}</EntityDrawer>
  • Do: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title={job.isError ? 'Job unavailable' : 'Loading job…'}>{body}</EntityDrawer>

Anti-slop

  • rule/entity-drawer-whatsapp-not-call: When the drawer shows a customer, put a "WhatsApp" action that opens whatsappHref(phone) in actions instead of a "Call" action on tel:, because customers are contacted by WhatsApp only and Call buttons were taken off every customer screen. Evidence: app 2/2 customer drawers carry WhatsApp and no Call, app/(app)/customers/customer-detail-panel.tsx:114, components/credits/customer-credit-sheet.tsx:109, the removal is the first left-out row of docs/restoration/README.md. Check: review, plus rg -n "tel:" app/(app)/customers components/credits.
  • Don't: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="Mama Put Kitchen" actions={<RowAction href="tel:08031234567">Call</RowAction>}>{body}</EntityDrawer>
  • Do: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="Mama Put Kitchen" actions={<RowAction href={whatsappHref(phone)} external>WhatsApp</RowAction>}>{body}</EntityDrawer>
  • rule/entity-drawer-stat-tone-state: When a stat's value is not in a real state (overdue, out, low, pending), leave tone unset instead of setting tone: 'good' to make a figure stand out, because status colour is kept for state and one green accent. Evidence: app 8/8 stat tones in the call sites are conditions on state, such as tone: overdue ? 'danger' : 'default' at app/(app)/customers/customer-detail-panel.tsx:130 and tone: openIssues > 0 ? 'warning' : 'default' at app/(app)/suppliers/supplier-drawer.tsx:46, found by rg -n "tone: " over the call-site files. Check: review.
  • Don't: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="Mama Put Kitchen" stats={[{ label: 'Lifetime spend', value: '₦1,240,000', tone: 'good' }]}>{body}</EntityDrawer>
  • Do: <EntityDrawer onClose={onClose} title="Mama Put Kitchen" stats={[{ label: 'Outstanding', value: '₦45,000', tone: overdue ? 'danger' : 'default' }]}>{body}</EntityDrawer>

Limits

Not applicable: no limit was measured this session. The tab count where tabs turn into a select on phones (3) is a constant in components/app/entity-drawer.tsx:76, not a measured break, so it stays out of Limits until a probe at 390px measures it.

Accessibility

Rests on the team's ModalDialog, a native <dialog> opened with the open attribute rather than showModal(), so toasts stay above it. The page behind is not inert.

Related

  • FormSheet: creating or editing a record through a form with a submit.
  • ConfirmDialog: the one confirm step a destructive overflow item opens.
  • OverflowMenu: holds the drawer's secondary and destructive actions.
  • SectionTabs: the drawer's section switcher.
  • StatusBadge: the status slot beside the title.
  • Skeleton: the bars the loading body draws.
  • DataTable: the list whose onRowClick opens the drawer.
  • PageHeader: the page title and actions behind the drawer; a record opens here, not as a page section.

FilterBar

Description

FilterBar narrows the list under it: a search box, a few inline filters, a "More filters" panel for rare ones, the active filters as removable chips, and the result count.

import { FilterBar, MoreFilterField, type FilterChip } from "@/components/app", source components/app/filter-bar.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: @base-ui/react Popover for the "More filters" panel, the rest hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/field-label (ARIA), trap/field-input-type (ARIA), trap/native-control (Foundation), trap/touch-input-zoom (States, finding), trap/overlay-title (ARIA), trap/overlay-focus-return (Keyboard), trap/overlay-conditional-render n/a because Popover.Root stays mounted and owns the open state, trap/escape-nested (Keyboard), trap/overlay-no-max-height (States), trap/open-trigger-unfocused (States), trap/focus-ring-shape (Keyboard, finding), trap/live-region-double (ARIA), trap/numbers-shift (Tokens), trap/hover-unguarded n/a because no hover rule changes display, visibility or opacity.

Example: Search for ingredients with one inline status filter and a result count (docs/system/examples/filter-bar/default.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { FilterBar } from '@/components/app';
import { FilterSelect } from '@/components/filter-select';

export default function FilterBarDefault() {
  const [q, setQ] = useState('');
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('all');
  return (
    <FilterBar
      search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ, placeholder: 'Search ingredients', label: 'Search ingredients' }}
      filters={
        <FilterSelect
          size="compact"
          ariaLabel="Stock status"
          value={status}
          onChange={setStatus}
          options={[
            { value: 'all', label: 'All stock' },
            { value: 'low', label: 'Low stock' },
          ]}
        />
      }
      resultLabel="24 ingredients"
    />
  );
}

Variants

moreColumns

  • true: the "More filters" panel is 42rem wide with two columns from sm up. The default when more holds 3 or more fields, counted through fragments. Used at 4 call sites by default (sales, suppliers, audit, POS transactions) and passed explicitly at 0.
  • false: the panel is 20rem wide with one stacked column. The default under 3 fields. Used at 4 call sites by default (churn, users, stock, POS shifts).

Example: Audit log bar whose More filters panel lays three fields out in two columns (docs/system/examples/filter-bar/more-columns-true.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { FilterBar, MoreFilterField } from '@/components/app';
import { FilterSelect } from '@/components/filter-select';

const ALL = [{ value: 'All', label: 'All' }];

export default function FilterBarMoreColumns() {
  const [q, setQ] = useState('');
  const [entity, setEntity] = useState('All');
  const [module, setModule] = useState('All');
  const [agent, setAgent] = useState('All');
  return (
    <FilterBar
      search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ, placeholder: 'Search by user or action', label: 'Search audit log' }}
      more={
        <>
          <MoreFilterField label="Record type">
            <FilterSelect ariaLabel="Record type" value={entity} onChange={setEntity} options={[...ALL, { value: 'Sale', label: 'Sale' }]} />
          </MoreFilterField>
          <MoreFilterField label="Module">
            <FilterSelect ariaLabel="Module" value={module} onChange={setModule} options={[...ALL, { value: 'pos', label: 'POS' }]} />
          </MoreFilterField>
          <MoreFilterField label="User">
            <FilterSelect ariaLabel="User" value={agent} onChange={setAgent} options={[...ALL, { value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Okafor' }]} />
          </MoreFilterField>
        </>
      }
      moreColumns
      moreActiveCount={[entity, module, agent].filter((v) => v !== 'All').length}
      resultLabel="1,204 entries"
    />

}

Example: Two active filters shown as removable chips, with Clear all and the result count (docs/system/examples/filter-bar/filtered.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { FilterBar, type FilterChip } from '@/components/app';

export default function FilterBarFiltered() {
  const [till, setTill] = useState<string | null>('Front till');
  const [q, setQ] = useState('jollof');
  const chips: FilterChip[] = [
    ...(till ? [{ key: 'till', label: `Till: ${till}`, onRemove: () => setTill(null) }] : []),
    ...(q ? [{ key: 'q', label: `"${q}"`, onRemove: () => setQ('') }] : []),
  ];
  return (
    <FilterBar
      search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ, placeholder: 'Search transactions', label: 'Search transactions' }}
      chips={chips}
      onClearAll={() => { setTill(null); setQ(''); }}
      resultLabel="18 transactions"
    />
  );
}

State precedence

  • More open and more active: both show. The badge stays on the trigger while the panel is open.
  • More open and trigger hover: more open wins. The trigger keeps its open fill when the pointer leaves.
  • Filtered and loading: both show. Chips stay while the count line is absent, so the person still sees what is filtering.
  • Rest and filtered: Not applicable: rest means the chip list is empty, filtered means it is not.
  • Searching and filtered: both show. A search chip joins the others once the caller adds it.

Props

FilterBar

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
chips?FilterChip[][]Active filters as removable chips.
className?string

MoreFilterField

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
childrenReactNode
labelstring
htmlFor?string
  • search takes value, onChange, placeholder and label. label names the field for screen readers; without it the placeholder is used, then "Search".
  • filters is a slot for 4 or fewer compact controls, per the JSDoc. Nothing enforces the cap.
  • more holds fields wrapped in MoreFilterField. Fragments are looked through when counting fields for moreColumns.
  • moreActiveCount is computed by the caller. The bar does not inspect more.
  • chips is a list of FilterChip (key, label, onRemove). "Clear all" renders only when chips is not empty and onClearAll is passed.
  • resultLabel sits in aria-live="polite", so every change is read aloud.
  • trailing is right-aligned with ml-auto on the first row.

Usage

When to use

  • A list or table screen where people narrow rows by search and by one to four common fields, with rarer fields one click away.
  • A dashboard or tab that needs location and period controls in one row above its content.

When not to use

  • Switching between whole sections of a page, not filtering one list. Use SectionTabs instead.
  • Picking only a date range with no list to filter. Use PeriodSelect on its own instead.
  • Two or three mutually exclusive views of the same list. Use Segmented instead.

Rules

  • rule/filter-bar-more-field: When a control goes inside more, wrap it in MoreFilterField with a label, because the panel gives the control no other visible label and the two-column grid sizes each wrapper as one cell. Evidence: app 8/8 bars that pass more wrap its fields in MoreFilterField (20 tags); principle heuristic: visible labels on every field. Check: review the more slot at each call site.
  • Don't: <FilterBar more={<FilterSelect ariaLabel="Till" value={till} onChange={setTill} options={tills} />} />
  • Do: <FilterBar more={<MoreFilterField label="Till"><FilterSelect ariaLabel="Till" value={till} onChange={setTill} options={tills} /></MoreFilterField>} />
  • rule/filter-bar-more-count: When more is passed, pass moreActiveCount with the number of fields in it that differ from their default, because a closed panel otherwise hides that rows are being filtered out. Evidence: app 8/8 bars with more pass moreActiveCount, such as app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:206; principle heuristic: visibility of system status. Check: review that more= and moreActiveCount= appear together.
  • Don't: <FilterBar more={tillField} />
  • Do: <FilterBar more={tillField} moreActiveCount={till ? 1 : 0} />
  • rule/filter-bar-clear-all: When chips can hold 2 or more chips, pass onClearAll too, because "Clear all" renders only when both are set and removing chips one by one takes one press each. Evidence: app 8/11 bars with chips pass onClearAll, strays app/(app)/inventory/requests-tab.tsx:144, app/(app)/inventory/stock-tab.tsx:176 and app/(app)/settings/users-section.tsx:117. Check: review.
  • Don't: <FilterBar chips={chips} />
  • Do: <FilterBar chips={chips} onClearAll={() => set({ till: null, cashier_id: null, q: null })} />

Content

  • rule/filter-bar-search-label: When search is passed, set search.label to "Search {records}" and the placeholder to the fields searched, because the placeholder disappears once someone types and the label is the field's only lasting name. Evidence: app 17/18 bars with search set a label apart from the placeholder, such as app/(app)/customers/page.tsx:185, stray app/(app)/pos/pos-filter-bar.tsx:29; principle wcag: 3.3.2 labels or instructions. Check: review.
  • Don't: <FilterBar search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ }} />
  • Do: <FilterBar search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ, placeholder: 'Search name, phone, email, company', label: 'Search customers' }} />
  • rule/filter-bar-chip-label: When a chip stands for a field filter, label it {Field}: {value} in sentence case, and a search chip "{query}" in quotes, because the chip row is the only place a filter set inside the closed panel stays visible. Evidence: app 9/11 chip builders use {Field}: {value} or "{query}", such as app/(app)/pos/transactions.tsx:54 and app/(app)/credits/page.tsx:150, strays app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:151 ("By {name}") and app/(app)/inventory/stock-tab.tsx:156 ("{n} SKUs"). Check: review.
  • Don't: { key: 'till', label: tillLabel(till), onRemove }
  • Do: { key: 'till', label: \Till: ${tillLabel(till)}\, onRemove }
  • rule/filter-bar-result-label: When resultLabel is passed, write {count} {noun} with the singular noun for 1, and pass undefined while the list loads, because the line is announced on every change and a stale "0 sales" during a fetch is read as a result. Evidence: single use components/app/filter-bar.tsx:80; app 6/6 counted callers pass undefined while loading, such as app/(app)/kitchen/jobs.tsx:210 and app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:210. Check: review.
  • Don't: <FilterBar resultLabel={\${rows.length} sales\} />
  • Do: <FilterBar resultLabel={list.data ? plural(rows.length, 'sale') : undefined} />

Anti-slop

  • rule/filter-bar-no-hand-row: When a list screen needs a search box beside filters, render FilterBar instead of a flex row with a raw <input type="search">, because the bar carries the sr-only label, the polite result line and the chip row that a hand-built row drops. Evidence: app 19/20 search boxes on list screens render through FilterBar, stray app/(app)/sales/sales-filter-bar.tsx:81 inside a picker. Check: lint rg -n 'type="search"' app components lib outside components/app/.
  • Don't: <div className="flex gap-2"><input type="search" value={q} onChange={(e) => setQ(e.target.value)} /></div>
  • Do: <FilterBar search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ, placeholder: 'Search recipes', label: 'Search recipes' }} />
  • rule/filter-bar-trailing-actions: When an action such as Export or a view toggle sits with the filters, pass it in trailing instead of filters, because trailing is pushed right with ml-auto and keeps actions apart from the controls that narrow the list. Evidence: single use components/app/filter-bar.tsx:76; app 5/19 bars pass actions in trailing, such as app/(app)/kitchen/jobs.tsx:199. Check: review.
  • Don't: <FilterBar filters={<><StatusFilter /><Button variant="outline">Export</Button></>} />
  • Do: <FilterBar filters={<StatusFilter />} trailing={<Button variant="outline">Export</Button>} />

Limits

Not applicable: the JSDoc cap of 4 inline filters is not measured yet at the narrowest width, so it is reported as a finding with a proposed gate instead of a rule.

Accessibility

Rests on a native <label> around <input type="search">, native <button> elements, and the Base UI Popover dialog.

FilterSelect

Description

FilterSelect picks one value from a short fixed list, as a list filter or as a form field, in an in-app menu that follows the theme.

import { FilterSelect } from "@/components/app", source components/filter-select.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: Select (base-nova, @base-ui/react) through components/ui/select.tsx. Traps checked: trap/native-control (Foundation), trap/field-label (ARIA, rule), trap/select-empty-value (Rules), trap/select-value-lost (State precedence), trap/overlay-no-max-height (States), trap/overlay-focus-return (Keyboard), trap/open-trigger-unfocused (States, finding), trap/control-height (Variants, rule), trap/focus-ring-shape (Tokens), trap/escape-nested (Keyboard), trap/select-async n/a because options arrive as a prop and nothing searches.

Example: A 40px form field for the product category, tied to its visible label by id (docs/system/examples/filter-select/default.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { FilterSelect } from '@/components/app';

const CATEGORIES = ['Fish', 'Poultry', 'Beef', 'Other'];

export default function FilterSelectDefault() {
  const [category, setCategory] = useState('Fish');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-1.5">
      <label htmlFor="example-category" className="text-sm font-medium">
        Category
      </label>
      <FilterSelect
        id="example-category"
        value={category}
        onChange={setCategory}
        options={CATEGORIES.map((c) => ({ value: c, label: c }))}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

Example: Two compact filters in the sales filter bar, beside search and the result count (docs/system/examples/filter-select/in-filter-bar.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { FilterBar } from '@/components/app/filter-bar';
import { FilterSelect } from '@/components/app';

export default function FilterSelectInFilterBar() {
  const [q, setQ] = useState('');
  const [agent, setAgent] = useState('');
  const [channel, setChannel] = useState('');
  return (
    <FilterBar
      search={{ value: q, onChange: setQ, placeholder: 'Search customer or sale ID', label: 'Search sales' }}
      filters={
        <>
          <FilterSelect
            size="compact"
            ariaLabel="Agent"
            value={agent || 'All'}
            onChange={(v) => setAgent(v === 'All' ? '' : v)}
            options={[
              { value: 'All', label: 'All agents' },
              { value: 'a1', label: 'Ada Okafor' },
              { value: 'a2', label: 'Tunde Bello' },
            ]}
          />
          <FilterSelect
            size="compact"
            ariaLabel="Channel"
            value={channel || 'All'}
            onChange={(v) => setChannel(v === 'All' ? '' : v)}
            options={[
              { value: 'All', label: 'All channels' },
              { value: 'WhatsApp', label: 'WhatsApp' },
              { value: 'Walk-in', label: 'Walk-in' },
            ]}
          />
        </>
      }
      resultLabel="1 to 50 of 812 sales"
    />
  );
}

Variants

size

  • default: 40px, full width, for a form field under its label. Used at 62 call sites, 45 of them overriding the height to 36px through className.
  • compact: 36px, w-auto, at least 10rem wide, for a FilterBar filters slot or a toolbar. Used at 2 call sites, the head-to-head pickers app/(app)/analytics/location-head-to-head.tsx:162; rule/filter-select-compact-size moves the hand-sized filters onto it.

Example: A 36px status filter with an All option first, mapped back to no filter in onChange (docs/system/examples/filter-select/size-compact.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { FilterSelect } from '@/components/app';

export default function FilterSelectCompact() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('');
  return (
    <FilterSelect
      size="compact"
      ariaLabel="Sale status"
      value={status || 'All'}
      onChange={(v) => setStatus(v === 'All' ? '' : v)}
      options={[
        { value: 'All', label: 'Any status' },
        { value: 'Paid', label: 'Paid' },
        { value: 'Part paid', label: 'Part paid' },
        { value: 'Unpaid', label: 'Unpaid' },
      ]}
    />
  );
}

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by

State precedence

  • Open and focused: open wins. Focus moves into the list, so the trigger loses its ring while the popup shows.
  • Value not in options and option selected: Not applicable: a value that matches no option leaves every option unselected.
  • Open and value not in options: both show. The empty trigger stays and the list opens with nothing checked.
  • Open and trigger hover: open wins. The dark hover fill applies, but the open popup is the only open cue.
  • Option highlighted and option selected: both show. The highlighted option gets the accent fill and the selected one keeps its check.
  • Closed after a refetch of options: the value wins. FilterSelect keeps whatever value the caller holds, and the label updates when the new options contain it.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Popup opens or closesannounceduration-100 with tw-animate-css fade-in-0, zoom-in-95 and slide-in-from-top-2 (components/ui/select.tsx)opacity, transformSame 100ms fade, zoom and slide. No prefers-reduced-motion rule in app/globals.css covers it (finding)

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
onChange(value: string) => void
optionsFilterOption[]
valuestring
ariaLabel?string
className?string""
icon?ReactNode
id?string
size?"default" | "compact""default"compact = 36px, for filter bars.
  • value is the selected option's value. Keep it inside options; see rule/filter-select-all-option.
  • onChange gets the picked option's value string, once per pick.
  • options is the list of { value, label }, rendered in order, as a FilterOption[].
  • size is default (40px, full width) or compact (36px, filter bars).
  • ariaLabel names the trigger when no visible label sits beside it.
  • id goes on the trigger, so a <label htmlFor> or FormField names it.
  • icon renders before the value inside the trigger.
  • className goes on the trigger and merges after the size classes, so it can override height and width.

Usage

When to use

  • A list screen filter with 2 to 30 fixed choices, such as status, agent, channel or record type.
  • A form field that picks one value from a fixed list, such as category or unit of measure.

When not to use

  • Choosing the location a screen reports on. Use LocationSelect instead.
  • Choosing a date window. Use PeriodSelect instead.
  • Two or three choices that should stay visible at once. Use Segmented instead.
  • Options that need groups, separators or custom item content. Use Select instead.

Rules

  • rule/filter-select-all-option: When a filter can be off, put a first option with a real value such as 'All' and map it to empty in onChange, because a value outside options shows the raw value, so '' renders an empty trigger with nothing checked and no way back to "no filter". Evidence: app 21/64 call sites carry an 'All' or 'all' option, such as app/(app)/sales/sales-filter-bar.tsx:43 and app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:193, and app/(app)/settings/sheet-select.tsx:18 maps '' to a sentinel for the same reason. Check: review that value falls back to the first option's value.
  • Don't: <FilterSelect ariaLabel="Agent" value={agent} onChange={setAgent} options={agents} />
  • Do: <FilterSelect ariaLabel="Agent" value={agent || 'All'} onChange={(v) => setAgent(v === 'All' ? '' : v)} options={[{ value: 'All', label: 'All agents' }, ...agents]} />
  • rule/filter-select-accessible-name: When FilterSelect renders, give it ariaLabel or an id that a <label htmlFor> points at, because the trigger is a combobox whose text is only the current value, so with neither it is announced as "Fish, combobox" with no field name. Evidence: app 64/64 call sites pass ariaLabel (33) or id (33), such as app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:185 and app/(app)/engagement/feedback-form.tsx:107. Check: review each <FilterSelect for ariaLabel= or id=.
  • Don't: <FilterSelect value={stage} onChange={setStage} options={STAGE_FILTERS} />
  • Do: <FilterSelect ariaLabel="Stage" value={stage} onChange={setStage} options={STAGE_FILTERS} />
  • rule/filter-select-compact-size: When FilterSelect sits in a FilterBar filters slot or a toolbar row, pass size="compact" instead of writing h-9 w-auto min-w-40 data-[size=default]:h-9 in className, because the hand-written classes drift in width (min-w-32, min-w-36, min-w-40) and break when the primitive's data-[size] height changes. Evidence: single use components/filter-select.tsx:33, the prop's own note "compact = 36px, for filter bars"; app 45/64 call sites set 36px by hand, such as app/(app)/kitchen/jobs.tsx:204 and app/(app)/inventory/stock-tab.tsx:181. Check: review className on each <FilterSelect for h-9.
  • Don't: <FilterSelect ariaLabel="Category" value={category} onChange={setCategory} options={options} className="h-9 w-auto min-w-40 data-[size=default]:h-9" />
  • Do: <FilterSelect size="compact" ariaLabel="Category" value={category} onChange={setCategory} options={options} />

Content

  • rule/filter-select-off-label: When the first option turns a filter off, label it "All {plural noun}" for a set of things or "Any {noun}" for a state, in sentence case, because the closed trigger shows only that label and it must read as "no filter" at a glance. Evidence: app 27/27 options with value 'All' or 'all' read "All ..." or "Any ...", such as "Any status" at app/(app)/sales/sales-filter-bar.tsx:40, "All channels" at app/(app)/sales/sales-filter-bar.tsx:46 and "All records" at app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:193. Check: review the first option's label.
  • Don't: { value: 'All', label: 'All' }
  • Do: { value: 'All', label: 'All channels' }

Anti-slop

  • rule/filter-select-no-empty-fallback: When a record's field can be missing, default value to a real option such as 'none' with the label "Choose a product" instead of ?? '', because '' matches no option and the field renders blank with no check. Evidence: app 60/64 call sites hold a value from their options, such as app/(app)/inventory/forms/form-bits.tsx:24 with 'none', and the 4 strays are app/(app)/inventory/forms/edit-sku-form.tsx:156, app/(app)/inventory/forms/edit-sku-form.tsx:159, app/(app)/inventory/forms/edit-sku-form.tsx:166 and app/(app)/inventory/forms/create-sku-form.tsx:295. Check: review ?? '' inside value= on a <FilterSelect.
  • Don't: <FilterSelect id="edit-category" value={product.category ?? ''} onChange={setCategory} options={CATEGORIES} />
  • Do: <FilterSelect id="edit-category" value={product.category ?? 'none'} onChange={setCategory} options={[{ value: 'none', label: 'Choose a category' }, ...CATEGORIES]} />

Limits

Not applicable: the popup caps at max-h-72 and scrolls, and no call site's option count or label width was measured at 390px this session, so no break point is known yet.
