OverflowMenu

Description

OverflowMenu holds the secondary and destructive actions of a page, a record or a row behind one ⋯ button, so the primary action can stand alone.

import { OverflowMenu, type OverflowItem } from "@/components/app", source components/app/overflow-menu.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: @base-ui/react Menu, wrapped in components/app/overflow-menu.tsx. Traps checked: trap/button-icon-name (ARIA: the trigger's name comes from label), trap/open-trigger-unfocused (States, Open: data-[popup-open]:bg-muted), trap/overlay-focus-return (Keyboard: Base UI returns focus to the trigger, and a finding for menus whose item removes the row), trap/menu-navigation (Rules: href items render Link or a, and a finding for items that call router.push), trap/menu-only-path (Rules: the trigger is a visible button, never hover or right-click), trap/menu-diagonal n/a because OverflowMenu has no submenus, trap/list-dead-gap (Tokens: items pad with py-1.5 and touch, the popup's p-1 is outside them), trap/escape-nested (Keyboard: by hand inside EntityDrawer), trap/exit-eats-input n/a because the popup has no exit animation, trap/scroll-chain n/a because the longest menu, 7 items in app/(app)/kitchen/job-panel.tsx:104, never scrolls, trap/touch-hover-flash (Tokens: Tailwind 4 hover: applies only under @media (hover: hover)), trap/loading-label-swap (States, a finding: 4 items swap their label while pending), trap/control-height (Rules: the two sizes match the buttons beside them), trap/weight-shift n/a because no state changes weight, trap/motion-transition-all n/a because the trigger names transition-colors.

Nothing for trigger sizesize of default (36px) or sm (32px), and label (default "More actions") as the trigger's aria-label and title

Variants

size

  • default: 36px square trigger (size-9), for page headers and drawer headers, beside 36px buttons. Used at 14 call sites.
  • sm: 32px square trigger (size-8), for table rows and settings lists, beside the 32px RowAction. Used at 11 call sites.

Example: Row menu at 32px for one supplier, named after the record, with Edit and a destructive Deactivate (docs/system/examples/overflow-menu/size-sm.tsx)

import { Ban, Pencil } from 'lucide-react';
import { OverflowMenu } from '@/components/app';

const noop = () => {};

      size="sm"

trigger

  • icon: no trigger prop, the ⋯ icon button, for secondary and destructive actions.
  • worded: trigger={{ text, icon, disabled }}, an outline button that shows its words, such as Download plus "Export", at the same 36px (or 32px) height, for a menu people come looking for. label stays its accessible name, and must start with the visible words ("Export suppliers"). disabled turns the whole trigger off, such as while an export runs. Used once, in hooks/use-export.ts:94.

State precedence

  • Open and Hover: Open wins. The trigger keeps the open fill when the pointer leaves.
  • Open and Focus visible: both show. Focus moves into the popup and the trigger keeps its open fill.
  • Item highlighted and Item disabled: Item disabled wins. The row dims and a press does nothing.
  • Destructive and Item highlighted: both show. Destructive text on the bg-destructive/10 fill.
  • Destructive and Item disabled: both show. Destructive text at 50% opacity.
  • Item pending and Item disabled: both show. The call site sets both at once.
  • All hidden and any other state: All hidden wins. Nothing renders, so no other state can be reached.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Trigger rest to hover, and rest to openannouncetransition-colors, Tailwind default 150msbackground-color, colorSame: a color change has no movement to remove
Popup closed to open, and open to closedannounceNone: the popup mounts and unmounts with no enter or exit animationnoneSame

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
itemsOverflowItem[]
className?string
label?string"More actions"
size?"default" | "sm""default"
trigger?OverflowTriggerShow a worded outline button, such as "Export", instead of ⋯.

gen-docs writes the table from the props type and OverflowItem.

  • items is the whole menu. Order inside each group is the array order; destructive items always follow the rest.
  • label defaults to "More actions" and becomes the trigger's aria-label and title.
  • size is default or sm.
  • trigger swaps the ⋯ for a worded button (see Variants). Leave it out for row, drawer and header menus.
  • className lands on the trigger. One call site uses it to shrink the trigger to 24px with no border.
  • Each OverflowItem takes onSelect or href, not both; external only matters with href; hidden removes the item; items are keyed by label, so two items with the same label collide (finding).

Usage

When to use

  • A page, drawer or row has actions beyond its one primary action, such as Import, Export, Template, Edit, Duplicate or Refresh
  • A record has destructive actions (Void, Deactivate, Delete, Archive, Cancel) that should sit behind one more press than the everyday ones

When not to use

  • The action is the page's or record's main next step, such as Record sale or Add customer. Use Button instead, in PageHeader actions
  • The person picks one value from a set, such as a period or a location. Use Segmented instead, or PeriodSelect and LocationSelect
  • A row has 1 or 2 everyday actions that people use on most visits. Use DataTable's RowAction instead, shown inline in the row

Rules

  • rule/overflow-menu-destructive-confirm: When an item has destructive: true, its onSelect opens ConfirmDialog naming the record instead of acting at once, because the menu closes on select and nothing offers an undo. Evidence: app 13/14 destructive items confirm first, through ConfirmDialog, a confirm panel or window.confirm, and the stray app/(app)/inventory/requests-tab.tsx:138 cancels the request at once. Check: review.
  • Don't: <OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Cancel request', destructive: true, onSelect: () => cancelRequest.mutateAsync(r._id) }]} />
  • Do: <OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Cancel request', destructive: true, onSelect: () => confirm('cancelRequest', r._id) }]} />
  • rule/overflow-menu-size-by-place: When the menu sits in a table row or a settings list, pass size="sm", and in a page header use the default size instead, because the trigger then matches the controls beside it: 32px RowAction in rows and 36px (h-9) buttons in headers. Evidence: app 8/8 table-row menus pass size="sm", app 7/7 page-header menus use the default size. Check: review.
  • Don't: <DataTable columns={[{ id: 'actions', header: '', cell: (s) => <OverflowMenu label={Actions for ${s.name}} items={items(s)} /> }]} />
  • Do: <DataTable columns={[{ id: 'actions', header: '', cell: (s) => <OverflowMenu size="sm" label={Actions for ${s.name}} items={items(s)} /> }]} />
  • rule/overflow-menu-hidden-flag: When an item depends on a permission or the record's state, set hidden on it instead of building the array with conditions, because OverflowMenu then returns null when nothing is left and no empty ⋯ reaches the screen. Evidence: app 18/25 call sites gate items with hidden, and none builds its items with a spread or .filter(); single use components/app/overflow-menu.tsx:32, the null return. Check: review.
  • Don't: <OverflowMenu items={[...(canVoid ? [{ label: 'Void sale', destructive: true, onSelect: voidSale }] : [])]} />
  • Do: <OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Void sale', destructive: true, onSelect: voidSale, hidden: !canVoid }]} />

Content

  • rule/overflow-menu-record-label: When the menu acts on one record, pass label as "Actions for {name}" or "More actions for {name}" instead of leaving the default "More actions", because in a table every trigger would otherwise share one accessible name. Evidence: app 10/11 per-record menus in rows and drawers name the record in label, and the stray app/(app)/inventory/requests-tab.tsx:132 reads "More request actions" in every row. Check: review.
  • Don't: <OverflowMenu size="sm" items={items(r)} />
  • Do: <OverflowMenu size="sm" label={Actions for ${r.name}} items={items(r)} />
  • rule/overflow-menu-item-sentence-case: When writing an item label, use sentence case, such as "Export sales" or "Void sale", instead of Title Case, because the label is the item's only name and the app's labels are sentence case (app/globals.css:10). Evidence: app 25/25 call sites use sentence-case item labels. Check: review.
  • Don't: <OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Export Sales', onSelect: exportSales }]} />
  • Do: <OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Export sales', onSelect: exportSales }]} />

Anti-slop

  • rule/overflow-menu-no-hand-menu: When a screen needs a ⋯ menu, render OverflowMenu instead of composing DropdownMenu or Base UI Menu with a MoreHorizontal trigger, because the hand-built one skips the hidden-item filter, the destructive group and the trigger sizes. Evidence: app 25/25 ⋯ menus outside components/app/ render OverflowMenu, and rg -n "MoreHorizontal|DropdownMenu" app components lib finds no other. Check: lint rg -n "MoreHorizontal" app components lib --glob '!components/app/overflow-menu.tsx' prints nothing.
  • Don't: <DropdownMenu><DropdownMenuTrigger><MoreHorizontal /></DropdownMenuTrigger><DropdownMenuContent>{items}</DropdownMenuContent></DropdownMenu>
  • Do: <OverflowMenu label="More sales actions" items={items} />
  • rule/overflow-menu-primary-outside: When an action is the page's or record's main next step, render it as a Button beside the menu instead of as the menu's first item, because inside the menu it takes 2 presses and gives no visible cue. Evidence: app 8/8 page headers with a primary keep it in PageHeader actions, and docs/restoration/kitchen-pos-settings-audit.md keeps the job's advance step as the primary button with the rest in the ⋯ menu. Check: review.
  • Don't: <OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Record sale', onSelect: openSale }, { label: 'Export sales', onSelect: exportSales }]} />
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Sales" actions={<Button onClick={openSale}>Record sale</Button>} overflow={<OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Export sales', onSelect: exportSales }]} />} />

Limits

  • Not applicable: no break was measured this session. The longest menu holds 7 items (app/(app)/kitchen/job-panel.tsx:104) and the popup has no max height; a probe on a 320px-tall screen is listed in the report.

Rests on the @base-ui/react Menu. The trigger is a button; the popup is a menu in a portal.

Related

  • PageHeader: holds the page's menu in overflow, after the primary action.
  • DataTable: its RowAction shows 1 or 2 everyday row actions inline, with OverflowMenu for the rest.
  • ConfirmDialog: what a destructive item opens before it acts.
  • EntityDrawer: holds a record's menu in its own overflow slot.

PageHeader

Description

PageHeader names the page a person is on, says in one line what they do there, and holds the page's own actions and section tabs.

import { PageHeader } from "@/components/app", source components/app/page-header.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/text-measure (Tokens: the description caps at max-w-[65ch]), trap/control-height (Rules: actions and the overflow trigger are both 36px at default size), trap/button-clone (Rules, a finding: every header with actions passes a hand-styled <button> or Link instead of Button), trap/native-control (same finding), trap/link-as-button (the Dashboard passes Links with button classes, app/(app)/_dashboard/dashboard-content.tsx:74), trap/button-label-wrap (States, Narrow: the cluster wraps whole buttons, and a finding: the hand-styled call-site buttons set no whitespace-nowrap, so a long label can wrap inside its button), trap/narrow-hidden-nav n/a because nothing clips: the cluster uses flex-wrap and the Dashboard folds its secondaries into the overflow menu below 640px, trap/current-unmarked n/a because tabs mark their own current item (SectionTabs spec), trap/safe-area and trap/viewport-height n/a because the header sits in the scrolling main, never at a fixed edge.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled. PageHeader is app code in components/app/page-header.tsx with no library primitive under it.

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
Nothing: a plain header, h1 and pTitle row with the action cluster on the right at 640px and up, stacked below it; overflow slot after actions; tabs slot under the title row

import { Download, FileSpreadsheet, Plus, Upload } from 'lucide-react';
import { PageHeader } from '@/components/app';
import { OverflowMenu } from '@/components/app/overflow-menu';
import { SectionTabs, type SectionTab } from '@/components/app/section-tabs';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';

const noop = () => {};
const tabs: SectionTab<'stock' | 'batches' | 'requests'>[] = [
  { id: 'stock', label: 'Stock' },
  { id: 'batches', label: 'Batches' },
  { id: 'requests', label: 'Requests' },
];

export default function PageHeaderInPage() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-5">
      <PageHeader
        title="Inventory"
        description="Stock, batches and expiry across your locations."
        actions={
          <Button onClick={noop}>
            <Plus aria-hidden /> Purchase stock
          </Button>
        }
        overflow={
          <OverflowMenu
            items={[
              { label: 'Create SKU', icon: <Plus />, onSelect: noop },
              { label: 'Import movements', icon: <Upload />, onSelect: noop },
              { label: 'Download import template', icon: <FileSpreadsheet />, onSelect: noop },
              { label: 'Export stock (CSV)', icon: <Download />, onSelect: noop },
            ]}
          />
        }
        tabs={<SectionTabs label="Inventory sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="stock" />}
      />
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Stock table goes here.</p>
    </div>
  );
}

Example: Customers header with one primary action and the secondary actions in the overflow menu (docs/system/examples/page-header/with-actions.tsx)

import { Download, FileSpreadsheet, Plus, Upload } from 'lucide-react';
import { PageHeader } from '@/components/app';
import { OverflowMenu } from '@/components/app/overflow-menu';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';

const noop = () => {};

export default function PageHeaderWithActions() {
  return (
    <PageHeader
      title="Customers"
      description="Find a customer, then message, sell or follow up."
      actions={
        <Button onClick={noop}>
          <Plus aria-hidden /> Add customer
        </Button>
      }
      overflow={
        <OverflowMenu
          label="More customer actions"
          items={[
            { label: 'Import customers', icon: <Upload />, onSelect: noop },
            { label: 'Download template', icon: <FileSpreadsheet />, onSelect: noop },
            { label: 'Export customers', icon: <Download />, onSelect: noop },
          ]}
        />
      }
    />
  );
}

import { PageHeader } from '@/components/app';

import { PageHeader } from '@/components/app';

const noop = () => {};

export default function PageHeaderOverflowAllHidden() {

State precedence

  • With actions and Narrow: both show. The cluster moves under the title and wraps.
  • With tabs and Narrow: both show. Tabs stay under everything else in the header.
  • With actions and With tabs: both show. The cluster stays in the title row, tabs below it.
  • Overflow all hidden and With actions: With actions wins. The cluster shows the actions controls only.
  • Title and description and the others: Not applicable: it is the base every other state adds to.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion. page-header.tsx has no transition or animation; motion inside the slots belongs to their own components.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
titlestring
actions?ReactNodeOne primary action, plus at most one secondary; everything else goes in overflow.
className?string
description?ReactNode
overflow?ReactNodeAn <OverflowMenu> for Import, Export, Template and the like.
tabs?ReactNode<SectionTabs>: always below the title, never in the action cluster.

gen-docs writes the table from PageHeaderProps.

  • title is a string and renders as the page's only h1.
  • description takes a node so the Dashboard can pass a date and a location, and Engagement a line per tab.
  • actions renders before overflow in one cluster, so the overflow trigger is always the last control.
  • tabs renders after the title row and never inside the cluster.
  • className lands on the header. No call site passes it.

Usage

When to use

  • A route under app/(app) needs its title, one line on what the page is for, and the page's own actions
  • A page splits into sections that the person switches between from the top of the page

When not to use

  • A record opened over a list, such as a customer or a supplier. Use EntityDrawer instead, which carries its own title and overflow
  • A side sheet with a form. Use FormSheet instead
  • A section title inside a page. Use SectionTabs instead when the sections switch, or a plain heading in the section's card

Rules

  • rule/page-header-one-primary: When actions is set, pass 1 primary action, placed last, and at most 1 secondary before it, and put every further action in overflow as an OverflowMenu instead, because the cluster is shrink-0 beside the title, so each extra button takes width from the title and description before anything wraps. Evidence: app 8/8 call sites with actions pass exactly 1 primary, 7/8 pass at most 1 secondary, stray app/(app)/_dashboard/dashboard-content.tsx:71 passes 2 secondaries at 640px and up; single use components/app/page-header.tsx:7, the JSDoc on actions states the same limit. Check: review.
  • Don't: <PageHeader title="Sales" actions={<><Button variant="outline">Import sales</Button><Button variant="outline">Export sales</Button><Button>Record sale</Button></>} />
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Sales" actions={<Button>Record sale</Button>} overflow={<OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Import sales', onSelect: importSales }, { label: 'Export sales', onSelect: exportSales }]} />} />
  • rule/page-header-tabs-slot: When a page has page-level sections, pass its SectionTabs through tabs instead of rendering it after PageHeader or inside actions, because tabs keeps the section switch inside the same header as the h1, under the title row at every width. Evidence: app 6/6 page-level SectionTabs on routes with a PageHeader go through tabs (Analytics, Kitchen, Inventory, POS, Engagement, Audit trail), and the other 2 SectionTabs are in-card filters at app/(app)/_dashboard/needs-attention.tsx:45 and app/(app)/engagement/interactions.tsx:207. Check: review.
  • Don't: <><PageHeader title="Inventory" /><SectionTabs label="Inventory sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="stock" /></>
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Inventory" tabs={<SectionTabs label="Inventory sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="stock" />} />
  • rule/page-header-one-per-route: When a route under app/(app) renders its main content, render 1 PageHeader as the first child of the page wrapper instead of a hand-written <h1>, because PageHeader holds the page's only h1 and screen reader users jump to it by heading. Evidence: app 12/12 main routes render exactly 1 PageHeader first; principle wcag: 2.4.6 Headings and labels, one h1 per page names its topic. Strays with their own h1: app/(app)/kitchen/board.tsx:185 (full-screen kitchen display), app/(app)/jobs/[id]/page.tsx:24 (job status page), and the access-required screens app/(app)/kitchen/page.tsx:28 and app/(app)/pos/page.tsx:33. Check: review.
  • Don't: <h1 className="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">Suppliers</h1>
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Suppliers" description="Find a supplier, check spend and open issues, then reorder." />

Content

  • rule/page-header-title-nav-label: When setting title, use the route's label from components/layout/nav-config.ts, in sentence case, 1 or 2 words, instead of a phrase or a verb, because the h1 confirms the sidebar item the person pressed. Evidence: app 12/12 titles equal their nav label (Dashboard, Analytics, Sales, POS, Credits, Customers, Engagement, Inventory, Suppliers, Kitchen, Audit trail, Settings). Check: review against components/layout/nav-config.ts.
  • Don't: <PageHeader title="Manage Your Customers" />
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Customers" />
  • rule/page-header-description-sentence: When setting a fixed description, write 1 sentence in sentence case that ends with a full stop and says what the person does on the page, instead of a slogan or a list of features, because the line is the page's only explanation and sits at max-w-[65ch]. Evidence: app 10/12 call sites pass one sentence with a full stop, and the 2 others are data, the Dashboard's date and location at app/(app)/_dashboard/dashboard-content.tsx:70 and Engagement's line per tab at app/(app)/engagement/page.tsx:59. Check: review.
  • Don't: <PageHeader title="Suppliers" description="Powerful supplier management" />
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Suppliers" description="Find a supplier, check spend and open issues, then reorder." />

Anti-slop

  • rule/page-header-no-eyebrow: When a page needs extra context, such as the location or the period, put it in description or the FilterBar under the header instead of an uppercase eyebrow, a breadcrumb or a badge above title, because labels in this app are sentence case with no uppercase micro labels (app/globals.css:10). Evidence: app 12/12 call sites render nothing above the title, and the Dashboard carries its location in description, app/(app)/_dashboard/dashboard-content.tsx:70. Check: review.
  • Don't: <><p className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wider">Lagos hub</p><PageHeader title="Dashboard" /></>
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Dashboard" description="Monday 23 November, Lagos hub" />
  • rule/page-header-overflow-last: When a page has secondary actions such as Import, Export, Template or Refresh, pass one OverflowMenu through overflow instead of a row of outline buttons, because the ⋯ trigger keeps the cluster to 2 or 3 controls and the restoration notes moved every such action there. Evidence: app 6/6 call sites with secondary file actions put them in overflow, and docs/restoration/sales-credits.md and docs/restoration/customers-engagement.md record Import and Export moving to the header ⋯ menu. Check: review.
  • Don't: <PageHeader title="Customers" actions={<><Button variant="outline">Import customers</Button><Button variant="outline">Export customers</Button></>} />
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Customers" overflow={<OverflowMenu items={[{ label: 'Import customers', onSelect: importCustomers }, { label: 'Export customers', onSelect: exportCustomers }]} />} />

Limits

  • Not applicable: no break was measured this session. The action count is held by rule/page-header-one-primary from call-site evidence, and the description width by max-w-[65ch] in code.

Accessibility

Rests on native header, h1 and p. PageHeader has no focusable part of its own; focus order is the slots' DOM order.

PeriodSelect

Description

PeriodSelect sets the date period a screen reports on, from a fixed preset list or a custom day range, in Lagos days.

import { PeriodSelect } from "@/components/app", source components/app/period-select.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: @base-ui/react Popover, with the app's own Calendar (components/app/calendar.tsx) and the period vocabulary in lib/period.ts. Traps checked: trap/overlay-title (ARIA, finding), trap/overlay-focus-return (Keyboard), trap/overlay-conditional-render n/a because Popover.Root stays mounted and the component owns open, trap/escape-nested n/a because nothing inside the popup opens a layer, trap/overlay-no-max-height (States), trap/open-trigger-unfocused (States), trap/select-value-lost (State precedence), trap/select-empty-value (Variants), trap/disabled-still-hovers (States, finding), trap/focus-ring-shape (Keyboard, finding), trap/field-label (ARIA), trap/current-unmarked (ARIA), trap/live-region-double (ARIA), trap/numbers-shift (Tokens).

Foundation

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
Popover.Root, Trigger, Portal, Positioner and Popup from @base-ui/react/popover: outside click and Escape to close, focus return, data-popup-open, --available-heightA controlled open that closes on a preset pick or Apply, and resets the draft range to the current value each time it opens
Calendar in mode="range" (team component): grid, arrow, PageUp, PageDown, Home and End keys, max to disable future daysThe preset column built from PERIOD_PRESETS, filtered by allowAll and presets, marked with SEGMENT_ACTIVE when selected
lib/period.ts (team): periodLabel, periodRange, lagosDay, parsePeriod, periodToParamsThe trigger text from periodLabel, a polite hint line under the calendar, and an Apply button enabled only for a complete range that differs from the current one

  • Sales list: app/(app)/sales/sales-filter-bar.tsx:26.

allowCustom

  • true: presets on the left and the range calendar with Apply on the right, stacked on phones. The default, used at 8 call sites.

Example: The audit log default, All time, where the range is open on both ends (docs/system/examples/period-select/all-time.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';

State precedence

  • Open and custom range applied: both show. The calendar opens on the applied range and no preset is selected.
  • Start picked and closed: closed wins. Closing drops the draft, and the next open starts from the applied range, so the applied value is never lost.
  • Range ready and apply disabled: Not applicable: range ready means the draft differs from the applied range, which is exactly when Apply is enabled.
  • Apply disabled and hover: hover wins in the code today, since hover:bg-primary/90 still applies to the disabled button (finding). The proposed fix makes apply disabled win.
  • Open and trigger hover: open wins. The trigger keeps its open fill and border.
  • Preset selected and custom range applied: Not applicable: value.preset holds one id, so a value is a preset or custom.

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
onChange(p: Period) => void

  • value is a Period from lib/period.ts: { preset }, or { preset: 'custom', from, to } with YYYY-MM-DD Lagos days.
  • onChange fires once per preset pick or Apply, never while picking days.
  • allowAll defaults to true. False drops "All time" from the list, for screens whose query needs a bounded range.
  • presets limits the preset list, such as ['today', '7d', '30d']. Order follows PERIOD_PRESETS, not this array.
  • allowCustom defaults to true. False drops the calendar and Apply.
  • className goes on the trigger.

Usage

When to use

  • A report, dashboard card or list whose numbers depend on a date window, where people mostly want a standard window and sometimes a custom one.

When not to use

  • Entering one date on a record, such as a delivery date. Use DateField instead.
  • Picking a day inside a form with no preset windows. Use Calendar inside DateField instead.
  • Switching between two or three fixed windows on a small card where a popup is too heavy. Use Segmented instead.

Rules

  • rule/period-select-url-params: When the screen's period belongs in the URL, write it with periodToParams and read it with parsePeriod using the same fallback, because the default preset is left out of the URL and a mismatched fallback turns a shared link into a different window. Evidence: app 2/2 URL call sites pair them, app/(app)/inventory/movements-tab.tsx:133 and app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:190 with fallback 'all'. Check: review the fallback argument on both calls.
  • Don't: <PeriodSelect value={parsePeriod(params, 'all')} onChange={(p) => set(periodToParams(p))} />
  • Do: <PeriodSelect value={parsePeriod(params, 'all')} onChange={(p) => set(periodToParams(p, 'all'))} />
  • rule/period-select-filter-slot: When a screen has a FilterBar, put PeriodSelect in its filters slot instead of beside the bar, because the bar wraps it with search and the other filters on phones. Evidence: app 6/8 call sites sit inside a FilterBar filters slot, such as app/(app)/customers/page.tsx:200, and the other two sit on screens with no FilterBar, app/(app)/analytics/page.tsx:96 and app/(app)/inventory/sales-trends.tsx:36. Check: review.
  • Don't: <div className="flex"><FilterBar search={search} /><PeriodSelect value={period} onChange={setPeriod} /></div>
  • Do: <FilterBar search={search} filters={<PeriodSelect value={period} onChange={setPeriod} />} />
  • rule/period-select-lagos-range: When a query or a filter needs the period's bounds, compute them with periodRange or inPeriod from lib/period.ts instead of new Date() arithmetic, because every period is counted in Lagos days and a browser in another zone shifts the window by a day. Evidence: single use lib/period.ts:16; principle heuristic: one source of truth for date windows. Check: review new Date( near period code.
  • Don't: const from = new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10)
  • Do: const { from, to } = periodRange(period)

Content

  • rule/period-select-preset-labels: When a period needs a name, take it from PERIOD_PRESETS or periodLabel ("Last 30 days", "This month", "1 Nov to 20 Nov") instead of writing new copy, because the same window must read the same on every screen. Evidence: app 8/8 call sites show periodLabel through the trigger; single use lib/period.ts:4. Check: review for period strings outside lib/period.ts.
  • Don't: <span>Past month</span>
  • Do: <span>{periodLabel(period)}</span>

Anti-slop

  • rule/period-select-no-second-picker: When a screen already has a PeriodSelect, keep one per screen instead of adding a second date picker for the same data, because two windows on one view make every KPI ambiguous. Evidence: app 8/8 files with a PeriodSelect render exactly one. Check: review.
  • Don't: <><PeriodSelect value={period} onChange={setPeriod} /><DateField label="From" value={from} onChange={setFrom} /></>
  • Do: <PeriodSelect value={period} onChange={setPeriod} />
  • rule/period-select-bounded-all: When the screen's query cannot run unbounded, pass allowAll={false} instead of mapping "All time" to a hidden cap, because the label "All time" then promises rows the query never fetches. Evidence: single use components/app/period-select.tsx:20; principle heuristic: match between system and the real world. Check: review queries that clamp from.
  • Don't: <PeriodSelect value={period} onChange={(p) => setPeriod(p.preset === 'all' ? { preset: '30d' } : p)} />
  • Do: <PeriodSelect value={period} onChange={setPeriod} allowAll={false} />

Limits

Not applicable: the preset list is fixed at 5 entries by PERIOD_PRESETS and the trigger label is at most "30 Nov to 30 Nov"; no count or length grows with data.

SectionErrorBoundary

Description

SectionErrorBoundary keeps one section's rendering failure inside that section, with a message and a way to try again, so the rest of the page keeps working.

import { SectionErrorBoundary } from "@/components/app", source components/app/error-boundary.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/toast-errors (States, Failed: the message stays until the person acts, never a toast), trap/color-only-status (States: the failure shows a triangle icon and "couldn't load" text, not only the destructive tint), trap/live-region-double (ARIA: each fallback is its own role="alert", and a finding for the Dashboard, where 6 can fire at once), trap/disabled-drops-focus (Keyboard, a finding: Try again unmounts itself and focus falls to the page body), trap/native-control and trap/button-clone (Tokens, a finding: Try again is a hand-styled <button>, not Button), trap/loading-layout-shift n/a because the boundary has no pending state, trap/loader-small-dots n/a because it shows no loader, trap/decor-pointer n/a because it draws no decorative layer, trap/reduced-motion-ignored n/a because nothing moves.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled. A React class component in components/app/error-boundary.tsx, with no library under it.

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
React's getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatchA fallback with the section's name, one line of guidance and Try again; resetKey, which clears the error when it changes; a console log tagged with the label

Example: Inventory tab body whose boundary clears when the active tab changes, so a failed tab does not stick (docs/system/examples/section-error-boundary/reset-by-key.tsx)

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { SectionErrorBoundary } from '@/components/app';
import { Segmented } from '@/components/app/segmented';

type Tab = 'stock' | 'batches';

function TabBody({ tab }: Readonly<{ tab: Tab }>) {
  if (tab === 'batches') throw new Error('Batches response was malformed');
  return <p className="text-sm">12 products below their minimum.</p>;
}

export default function SectionErrorBoundaryResetByKey() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState<Tab>('stock');
  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <Segmented
        label="Inventory sections"
        value={tab}
        onChange={setTab}
        options={[
          { id: 'stock', label: 'Stock' },
          { id: 'batches', label: 'Batches' },
        ]}
      />
      <SectionErrorBoundary label="Inventory" resetKey={tab}>
        <TabBody tab={tab} />
      </SectionErrorBoundary>
    </div>
  );
}

State precedence

  • Failed and Reset by key: Reset by key wins. A new resetKey clears the error before the next render, so the new tab never inherits the old failure.
  • Failed and Retried: Failed wins when the children throw again. The card comes back at once.
  • Unlabelled and Failed: both show. Unlabelled only changes the title text.
  • Healthy and Failed: Not applicable: the boundary holds one or the other.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion. error-boundary.tsx has no transition or animation, and the card appears in one frame.

Props

gen-docs writes the table from Props in components/app/error-boundary.tsx.

  • label names the section in the title, "{label} couldn't load", and tags the console log.
  • resetKey is compared on every render; any change clears the error. 11 call sites pass it.
  • children is the section. Only errors thrown while rendering it are caught, not errors in event handlers or rejected requests that the section handles itself.

Usage

When to use

  • A section of a page renders data from its own request, such as a KPI strip, a chart, a list or a tab's body, and a bad response there should not blank the page
  • A drawer or panel shows one record in tabs, and one tab's failure should leave the others usable

When not to use

  • A request failed and the section knows it, such as a query in an error state. Use EmptyState instead, in the section, with the retry the section owns
  • A list loaded and has no rows. Use EmptyState instead
  • A form submit failed. Use FormSheet instead, which keeps the input and shows the error on the form

Rules

  • rule/section-error-boundary-reset-key: When the boundary wraps content that changes with a tab, a page of results or a record, pass that value as resetKey instead of leaving it out or remounting with key, because without it the Failed card stays after the person moves to content that would render. Evidence: app 11/12 boundaries around tabbed, filtered, paged or per-record content pass resetKey, and the stray app/(app)/sales/page.tsx:167 wraps the paged sales list with none; single use app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:59 also passes key, which remounts the boundary and its children on every tab change. Check: review.
  • Don't: <SectionErrorBoundary label="Inventory">{tab === 'stock' ? <StockTab /> : <BatchesTab />}</SectionErrorBoundary>
  • Do: <SectionErrorBoundary label="Inventory" resetKey={tab}>{tab === 'stock' ? <StockTab /> : <BatchesTab />}</SectionErrorBoundary>
  • rule/section-error-boundary-per-section: When a page shows sections that load on their own, such as KPIs, charts and lists, wrap each section in its own SectionErrorBoundary instead of one around the whole page, because one bad response then replaces only its own section. Evidence: app 22/22 boundaries wrap one section or one tab's body and none wraps a route, with 6 on the Dashboard and 3 on the POS overview; single use components/app/error-boundary.tsx:15, the JSDoc states the same job. Check: review.
  • Don't: <SectionErrorBoundary label="Dashboard"><DashboardKpis /><SalesChart /><TopCustomers /></SectionErrorBoundary>
  • Do: <><SectionErrorBoundary label="Key figures"><DashboardKpis /></SectionErrorBoundary><SectionErrorBoundary label="Sales"><SalesChart /></SectionErrorBoundary></>

Content

  • rule/section-error-boundary-label: When setting label, pass the section's name as a sentence-case noun phrase that reads before "couldn't load", such as "Customer list" or "Key figures", instead of leaving it out, because without it the title reads "This section couldn't load" and does not say which part failed. Evidence: app 22/22 call sites pass label, 19 as a fixed noun phrase and 3 from the active tab's name. Check: review.
  • Don't: <SectionErrorBoundary><CustomerTable /></SectionErrorBoundary>
  • Do: <SectionErrorBoundary label="Customer list"><CustomerTable /></SectionErrorBoundary>

Anti-slop

  • rule/section-error-boundary-no-hand-boundary: When a section needs an error fallback, wrap it in SectionErrorBoundary instead of writing another class with getDerivedStateFromError or a try and catch around JSX, because a second boundary drifts from this copy, this card and resetKey. Evidence: app 22/22 error fallbacks outside components/app/ use SectionErrorBoundary, and grep -rn "getDerivedStateFromError" app components lib finds only components/app/error-boundary.tsx. Check: lint grep -rn "getDerivedStateFromError\|componentDidCatch" app components lib prints only components/app/error-boundary.tsx.
  • Don't: class ChartBoundary extends Component { static getDerivedStateFromError() { return { failed: true }; } }
  • Do: <SectionErrorBoundary label="Revenue by category"><CategoryChart /></SectionErrorBoundary>
  • rule/section-error-boundary-no-raw-message: When the fallback shows, keep its fixed copy instead of adding the caught error.message or a stack to the card, because the message is written for the person and the details go to the console under the label. Evidence: single use components/app/error-boundary.tsx:32 logs the error with the label and components/app/error-boundary.tsx:45 shows fixed guidance; principle heuristic: Nielsen's "help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors" asks for plain language and a way out, not a code. Check: review.
  • Don't: <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{this.state.error.message}</p>
  • Do: <SectionErrorBoundary label="Payment mix"><PaymentMix /></SectionErrorBoundary>

Limits

  • Not applicable: the boundary has no count, length or size to grow. How many boundaries share a page is held by rule/section-error-boundary-per-section.

SectionTabs

Description

SectionTabs switches between the sections of one page, keeps the chosen section in the URL so it can be linked, and turns into a select on phones.

import { SectionTabs, useSectionTab, type SectionTab } from "@/components/app", source components/app/section-tabs.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled tablist on native <button> elements, with FilterSelect (components/filter-select.tsx) as the phone fallback and useUrlState (hooks/use-url-state.ts) for ?tab=. Traps checked: trap/tabs-routes (Usage, Accessibility), trap/current-unmarked (ARIA), trap/weight-shift (States), trap/narrow-hidden-nav (States), trap/list-dead-gap (Tokens), trap/focus-ring-shape (Keyboard), trap/link-as-button n/a because every tab is a <button> and none navigates to another route, trap/touch-hover-flash n/a because Tailwind v4 wraps hover: in @media (hover: hover), trap/numbers-shift (Tokens).

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled.

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
Not applicable: hand-rolled, no tabs primitive underneathrole="tablist" with role="tab" buttons, roving tabIndex, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight that wrap, Home and End, an underline for the active tab, count badges with three tones, hidden tabs, URL mode through useUrlState, controlled mode through value and onChange, and a FilterSelect below md unless inlineOnMobile
Not applicable: hand-rolleduseSectionTab, which reads ?tab= (or param) and falls back to defaultTab when the value is missing, unknown or hidden

Example: Kitchen sections synced to ?tab=, with the board as the default tab (docs/system/examples/section-tabs/default.tsx)

'use client';

import { SectionTabs, useSectionTab, type SectionTab } from '@/components/app';

const SECTIONS: SectionTab<'board' | 'jobs' | 'recipes'>[] = [
  { id: 'board', label: 'Board' },
  { id: 'jobs', label: 'Jobs' },
  { id: 'recipes', label: 'Recipes' },
];

export default function SectionTabsDefault() {
  const section = useSectionTab(SECTIONS, 'board');
  return (
    <div>
      <SectionTabs label="Kitchen sections" tabs={SECTIONS} defaultTab="board" />
      <p className="pt-4 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Showing {section}</p>
    </div>
  );
}

'use client';

import { SectionTabs, type SectionTab } from '@/components/app';

const TABS: SectionTab<'stock' | 'movements' | 'requests'>[] = [

Variants

inlineOnMobile

  • true: the tab bar shows at every width and scrolls sideways when it overflows. For 2 to 3 short tabs, per the JSDoc. Used at 1 call site, app/(app)/engagement/page.tsx:63.
  • false: below md (768px) the bar hides and a FilterSelect named by label takes its place, with counts in the option text as "{label} ({count})". Used at 7 call sites by default.

'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { SectionTabs } from '@/components/app';

export default function SectionTabsInlineOnMobile() {

  return (

State precedence

  • Active tab and hover: active wins. The primary underline and foreground text stay under the pointer.
  • Active tab and focus visible: both show. The outline draws over the underline.
  • Hidden tab and active: hidden wins. A hidden id in the URL is treated as unknown, so defaultTab becomes active.
  • With count and active: both show. The badge keeps its tone on the active tab.
  • Phone select and overflow: phone select wins. Below md the bar is hidden, so it cannot overflow there.
  • Inactive tab and active tab: Not applicable: each tab is one or the other.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Hover, or a tab becoming activeinputtransition-colors (Tailwind default 150ms, no app preset exists in app/globals.css)color, border-colorSame 150ms colour change. Nothing moves

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
labelstring
tabsSectionTab<T>[]
className?string
defaultTab?T
inlineOnMobile?booleanKeep the tab bar on phones instead of switching to a select (for 2 to 3 short tabs).
onChange?((id: T) => void)
param?string

  • tabs is a list of SectionTab: id, label, optional count, countTone ("neutral", "warning" or "danger") and hidden.
  • label names the tablist and the phone select. It is required.
  • URL mode: pass defaultTab and optionally param (default "tab"). Picking the default tab removes the param from the URL. Read the same value with useSectionTab(tabs, defaultTab, param).
  • Controlled mode: pass value and onChange. The types forbid mixing the two modes.
  • inlineOnMobile keeps the bar on phones.
  • className goes on the outer wrapper that draws the bottom border.

Usage

When to use

  • A page with two or more sections under one title, where each section is a separate view the person may link to or reload into.
  • A card or drawer that splits its content into a few groups with counts, such as the dashboard's needs attention card.

When not to use

  • Narrowing the rows of one list by a field. Use FilterBar instead.
  • Two or three views of the same data in a small space, such as a chart's range. Use Segmented instead.
  • Moving to another route. Use a link in the sidebar or page header instead, since a tab here is a button that never navigates (trap/tabs-routes). Use PageHeader actions for that link instead.

Rules

  • rule/section-tabs-same-default: When a bar uses URL mode, read the active tab with useSectionTab passing the same defaultTab and param as the bar, because the bar and the panel otherwise disagree on which section is open when the URL has no tab. Evidence: app 6/6 URL-mode bars pair them, such as app/(app)/kitchen/page.tsx:55 with app/(app)/kitchen/page.tsx:124. Check: review both calls side by side.
  • Don't: const tab = useSectionTab(tabs, 'stock'); <SectionTabs label="Inventory sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="movements" />
  • Do: const tab = useSectionTab(tabs, 'stock'); <SectionTabs label="Inventory sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="stock" />
  • rule/section-tabs-nested-param: When a URL-mode bar sits inside a section of another URL-mode bar, pass a distinct param such as "view", because both default to ?tab= and the inner bar would switch the page's section. Evidence: single use app/(app)/engagement/interactions.tsx:185. Check: review pages with two SectionTabs tags.
  • Don't: <SectionTabs label="Interaction types" tabs={views} defaultTab="feedback" />
  • Do: <SectionTabs label="Interaction types" tabs={views} param="view" defaultTab="feedback" />
  • rule/section-tabs-local-controlled: When tabs sit inside a card or drawer, or a tab change must also reset other URL params, pass value and onChange instead of defaultTab, because URL mode writes only its own param. Evidence: app 2/2 controlled bars, app/(app)/_dashboard/needs-attention.tsx:45 (a card) and app/(app)/pos/page.tsx:50 (clears the tab's filters in one set). Check: review.
  • Don't: <SectionTabs label="Needs attention" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="overdue" />
  • Do: <SectionTabs label="Needs attention" tabs={tabs} value={tab} onChange={setPicked} />
  • rule/section-tabs-hide-not-remove: When a person may not see a section, pass the tab with hidden: true instead of filtering the array at the call site, because useSectionTab then treats a linked ?tab= for it as unknown and falls back to defaultTab. Evidence: single use app/(app)/engagement/page.tsx:36; single use components/app/section-tabs.tsx:30. Check: review.
  • Don't: <SectionTabs label="Engagement sections" tabs={canSee ? tabs : tabs.slice(0, 1)} defaultTab="overview" />
  • Do: <SectionTabs label="Engagement sections" tabs={[{ id: 'interactions', label: 'Interactions', hidden: !canSee }]} defaultTab="overview" />

Content

  • rule/section-tabs-label: When rendering SectionTabs, set label to the name of the group, "{Page} sections" for a page header bar, because it names the tablist and the phone select, and a screen reader hears it before the first tab. Evidence: app 6/6 page header bars use "{Page} sections", such as app/(app)/audit/page.tsx:185. Check: review.
  • Don't: <SectionTabs label="Tabs" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="all" />
  • Do: <SectionTabs label="Audit sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="all" />

Anti-slop

  • rule/section-tabs-count-tone: When a tab count stands for items that need action, set countTone to "warning" for pending or low and "danger" for overdue or out, and leave other counts "neutral", because status colour is reserved for real state. Evidence: single use app/globals.css:11; app 9/9 countTone values follow it, such as app/(app)/_dashboard/needs-attention.tsx:29. Check: review countTone values.
  • Don't: { id: 'recipes', label: 'Recipes', count: 12, countTone: 'warning' }
  • Do: { id: 'recipes', label: 'Recipes', count: 12 }
  • rule/section-tabs-no-hand-tablist: When a page needs sections under its title, render SectionTabs in the PageHeader tabs slot instead of a hand-built role="tablist" row, because the hand-built row misses the URL sync, the phone select and the count tones. Evidence: app 6/7 section tab rows under a title use it, stray app/(app)/kitchen/board.tsx:248 (board stage). Check: lint rg -n 'role="tablist"' app components lib outside components/app/.
  • Don't: <div role="tablist"><button role="tab" aria-selected={tab === 'stock'}>Stock</button></div>
  • Do: <PageHeader title="Inventory" tabs={<SectionTabs label="Inventory sections" tabs={tabs} defaultTab="stock" />} />

Limits

Not applicable: the JSDoc says inlineOnMobile suits 2 to 3 short tabs, but no overflow width was measured this session, so the cap is reported as a finding with a proposed gate instead of a rule.

Accessibility

Rests on native <button> elements with role="tab" inside a role="tablist", and on the Base UI Select inside FilterSelect below md.

Related

Skeleton

Description

Skeleton holds the place of content that is still loading, at the size and shape that content will take, so the screen does not jump when it arrives.

import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton", source components/ui/skeleton.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: shadcn skeleton (base-nova, base). Traps checked: trap/loading-layout-shift (Rules), trap/reduced-motion-ignored (Motion: skeleton-shimmer stops the pulse), trap/motion-layout-property (Motion: opacity only), trap/motion-linear n/a because the pulse eases with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1), trap/loop-offscreen (Motion, NEEDS REVIEW: the pulse is a CSS loop that is not paused off screen, not measured), trap/live-region-double (ARIA: Skeleton announces nothing, its wrapper does), trap/illustration-announced (ARIA: an empty div is read as nothing), trap/loader-small-dots n/a because Skeleton draws bars, not dots, trap/loading-label-swap n/a because Skeleton carries no label, trap/decor-pointer n/a because Skeleton sits in flow, never over a control, trap/color-only-status, trap/numbers-shift, trap/toast-errors, trap/toast-timer, trap/motion-restart, trap/motion-blocks-input and trap/demo-on-timers n/a because Skeleton holds no status, number, message, trigger or demo.

Foundation

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
shadcn skeleton for style base-nova (components.json), base base: a div with data-slot="skeleton" and animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted, forwarding every div propThe fill is bg-muted/80 instead of bg-muted, a lighter bar on the app's tinted surfaces. Found by diffing against npx shadcn@latest view skeleton this session
No reduced-motion handling of its ownThe skeleton-shimmer class, a hook that app/globals.css:299 stops under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. It carries no styles otherwise
The cn import from the registry's cnRewritten to @/lib/utils, single quotes and semicolons, from the project's formatting

Variants

Not applicable: Skeleton has no variant props. Size, width and radius come from className at each call site.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
PulsingMounted while its content loadsWait. Nothing in it is interactiveOpacity pulses between 100% and 50% every 2s (animate-pulse)screenshot
Reduced motionThe OS asks for reduced motionWaitA still bar at full opacity, since .skeleton-shimmer { animation: none }by hand
ShapedThe caller passes the target's radius, such as rounded-full or rounded-xlWaitThe bar's outline matches the avatar or card it stands forscreenshot
ReplacedThe data arrives and the caller renders the contentUse the contentThe bar is gone. Whether the box keeps its height depends on the caller's height class (trap/loading-layout-shift)by hand

Example: One block skeleton at the chart's own height, h-40, while ranked bars load (docs/system/examples/skeleton/chart-block.tsx)

import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton';

    </div>

}

State precedence

  • Pulsing and reduced motion: reduced motion wins. The bar stays still at full opacity.
  • Shaped and pulsing: both show.
  • Replaced and any other state: replaced wins, since the caller unmounts the Skeleton.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Mounted, loops until unmountedannounceanimate-pulse, Tailwind's 2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) infinite, no named presetopacityNo animation, a still bar (app/globals.css:299)

Props

No props of its own.

Also accepts: native element attributes from React's types.

gen-docs writes the table from React.ComponentProps<'div'>. Skeleton adds no props of its own.

  • className: sets the height, width and radius of the bar. Every call site passes at least a height.

Usage

When to use

  • A region whose content is still loading and whose size is known in advance, such as a chart, a KPI value, a table row or a list of cards.

When not to use

  • A whole table, card, chart or panel that already has a loading layout. Use LoadingSkeletons instead.
  • A record drawer that is loading. Use EntityDrawer with loading instead.

Rules

  • rule/skeleton-set-height: When a Skeleton stands in for content, pass a height class in className, such as h-40 w-full for a 160px chart or h-4 w-24 for a line of text, instead of a bare <Skeleton />, because Skeleton is an empty div and draws 0px tall without one, so nothing shows and the content pushes the layout when it lands. Evidence: app 27/27 call sites pass a height or size class (h-* or size-*), found by rg -n "<Skeleton" app components lib --glob '!components/ui/**'; principle platform: an empty block div has a content height of 0. Check: review.
  • Don't: {loading ? <Skeleton /> : <RankedBars rows={bestSellers} format={formatMoneyShort} />}
  • Do: {loading ? <Skeleton className="h-40 w-full" /> : <RankedBars rows={bestSellers} format={formatMoneyShort} />}
  • rule/skeleton-shape-radius: When a Skeleton stands for an avatar or a card, give it that element's radius, rounded-full for an avatar and rounded-xl for a card, instead of the default rounded-md, because the bar should outline what replaces it and the app's radius rule gives cards rounded-xl and avatars rounded-full. Evidence: app 3/3 avatar or card skeletons carry the target radius, app/(app)/engagement/churn.tsx:198, app/(app)/engagement/churn.tsx:205, app/(app)/engagement/churn.tsx:207. Check: review.
  • Don't: <Skeleton className="size-12" />
  • Do: <Skeleton className="size-12 rounded-full" />

Content

Not applicable: Skeleton renders no text. The loading name, such as "Loading customer details", belongs to the wrapping status region, which is the caller's.

Anti-slop

  • rule/skeleton-not-raw-pulse: When a screen needs a loading placeholder, render Skeleton instead of a hand-made div with animate-pulse bg-muted, because a raw copy misses the skeleton-shimmer hook and keeps pulsing under reduced motion. Evidence: app 27/28 pulse placeholders outside the ui folder use Skeleton, stray app/(app)/pos/overview.tsx:103, found by rg -n "animate-pulse" app components lib. Check: review, plus rg -n "animate-pulse" app components lib --glob '!components/ui/**'.
  • Don't: <div className="h-8 animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted" />
  • Do: <Skeleton className="h-8" />

Limits

Not applicable: no bar count or size limit was measured this session. Real call sites draw 1 to 5 bars per region.

Accessibility

Rests on a plain div with no role. Skeleton is silent by itself, so the caller's wrapper announces loading. Today 2 of the 19 loading regions outside the ui folder wrap their Skeletons in role="status" with a name (components/app/entity-drawer.tsx:83, app/(app)/engagement/churn.tsx:198), and 1 sets aria-busy only (app/(app)/_dashboard/sales-panel.tsx:61); the rest are silent (finding).

Related

  • LoadingSkeletons: ready-made table, card, chart and panel loading layouts built from Skeleton.
  • EntityDrawer: draws three Skeleton bars when loading is set.
  • KpiStrip: draws Skeleton bars per cell while figures load.
  • DataTable: draws Skeleton cells while rows load.
  • EmptyState: what replaces the skeleton when loading ends with no rows.

StatusBadge

Description

StatusBadge names the state a record is in, such as Paid, Low or Resolved, in one word or two, with a tone that says how much it needs attention.

import { StatusBadge, STATUS_TONES, type Tone } from "@/components/app", source components/app/status-badge.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/color-only-status (States and Accessibility: the state word is always the badge's text), trap/numbers-shift answered by the caller: the one badge whose label is a live due time, app/(app)/kitchen/board.tsx:310, passes tabular-nums through className, and the component itself sets none (finding in the run report), trap/empty-value n/a because a missing status renders no badge at the call sites rather than an empty one, trap/table-divs, trap/list-dead-gap, trap/narrow-hidden-nav n/a because it is an inline label, not a table, list or nav, trap/icon-optical-size and trap/icon-optical-align n/a because no call site puts an icon in a badge, trap/loading-layout-shift, trap/loading-label-swap, trap/loader-small-dots n/a because it has no loading state, trap/toast-errors, trap/toast-timer, trap/live-region-double n/a because it is not a toast and has no live region, trap/decor-pointer n/a because it is not interactive and sets no pointer cursor, trap/demo-on-timers, trap/reduced-motion-ignored, trap/loop-offscreen, trap/motion-restart, trap/motion-layout-property, trap/motion-blocks-input n/a because it has no motion.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled. A span with five tone classes and the STATUS_TONES table in components/app/status-badge.tsx, with no shadcn Badge underneath.

Example: In a DataTable status column, placed in the phone card's meta line (docs/system/examples/status-badge/in-data-table.tsx)

import { StatusBadge } from "@/components/app";
import { DataTable, type Column } from "@/components/app/data-table";

type Sale = { id: string; customer: string; status: string };
const rows: Sale[] = [
  { id: "s1", customer: "Mama Put Kitchen", status: "Paid" },
  { id: "s2", customer: "Ada Foods", status: "Overdue" },
];
const columns: Column<Sale>[] = [
  { id: "customer", header: "Customer", cell: (r) => r.customer, mobile: "title" },
  { id: "status", header: "Status", cell: (r) => <StatusBadge domain="payment" status={r.status} />, mobile: "meta" },
];

export default function Example() {
  return <DataTable label="Sales" columns={columns} rows={rows} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />;
}

Variants

The two axes are exclusive: a call passes domain with status, or tone with children, never both (the props type is a union).

tone

  • neutral: a label that is not a state of concern, such as a category, a channel or "Voided". Used at 30 call sites.
  • good: paid, in stock, resolved, approved, fulfilled. Used at 10 call sites.
  • warning: pending, low, partial, unpaid, expiring soon. Used at 12 call sites.
  • danger: overdue, out, expired, rejected, failed. Used at 3 call sites.
  • info: an outlined badge on the page background. Used at 0 call sites.

25 more call sites compute the tone from the record, such as expiryTone(b.expiryDate) or due.tone === 'overdue' ? 'danger' : 'warning'.

domain

  • payment: a sale's or job's payment state: Paid, Partial, Credit, Unpaid, Overdue, Voided. Used at 4 call sites.
  • stock: a product's stock state: In stock, Low, Out, Expiring, Expired. Used at 4 call sites.
  • work: a ticket's or request's state: Open, Pending, In progress, Approved, Fulfilled, Resolved, Rejected, Closed. Used at 8 call sites.

Not applicable: a badge holds one status, and the props union lets a call pass a domain status or a custom label, never both.

Not applicable: no motion.

gen-docs writes the table from the types.

  • domain and status look the tone up in STATUS_TONES, exported beside the component.
  • tone with children sets the tone and text directly.
  • className is passed at 2 call sites, one of them capitalize at app/(app)/customers/customer-import-summary.tsx:65, which breaks sentence case.

Usage

When to use

  • A row, card or drawer shows the state of one record, such as a sale's payment, a product's stock or a ticket's progress
  • A short neutral tag beside a record names its category or channel

When not to use

  • A headline count of records in a state, such as "12 overdue". Use KpiStrip instead
  • A whole list has nothing in a state. Use EmptyState instead
  • A choice the person makes between states. Use Segmented instead

Rules

  • rule/status-badge-domain-first: When the status is a payment, stock or work word listed in STATUS_TONES, pass domain and status instead of tone with a local mapping, because the shared table keeps one tone per word on every screen. Evidence: app 16/20 call sites that show a STATUS_TONES word pass domain, with strays app/(app)/customers/customer-interactions-tab.tsx:62, app/(app)/customers/customer-interactions-tab.tsx:81, app/(app)/customers/customer-interactions-tab.tsx:100 (a local workTone) and app/(app)/kitchen/kitchen-ui.tsx:45 (a local PAYMENT_TONE). Check: review.
  • Don't: <StatusBadge tone={f.status === 'Open' ? 'warning' : 'good'}>{f.status}</StatusBadge>
  • Do: <StatusBadge domain="work" status={f.status} />
  • rule/status-badge-tone-meaning: When picking a tone, use danger for overdue, out, expired or failed, warning for pending, low, partial or expiring, good for paid, in stock or resolved, and neutral for everything else, instead of choosing a tone for emphasis, because status colour is kept for real state and every other label stays neutral. Evidence: principle heuristic: consistency of signals, written as the visual rule at app/globals.css:11 and the doc comment at components/app/status-badge.tsx:15; app 30/55 literal tones are neutral and the 25 others follow the mapping, read from the props of each <StatusBadge tag. Check: review.
  • Don't: <StatusBadge tone="good">Retail</StatusBadge>
  • Do: <StatusBadge tone="neutral">Retail</StatusBadge>

Content

  • rule/status-badge-label-case: When writing the label, use 1 to 3 words in sentence case, such as "In stock", "Part paid" or "Expires in 3 days", instead of capitals or Title Case, because the visual rules set every label in sentence case and the badge is read in a table scan. Evidence: app 19/19 STATUS_TONES keys are in sentence case (components/app/status-badge.tsx:19), with one stray className="capitalize" at app/(app)/customers/customer-import-summary.tsx:65. Check: review.
  • Don't: <StatusBadge tone="warning" className="uppercase">PART PAID</StatusBadge>
  • Do: <StatusBadge tone="warning">Part paid</StatusBadge>

Anti-slop

  • rule/status-badge-no-colour-class: When a badge needs a different colour, pick another tone instead of passing colour classes through className, because the five tones hold the only status colours and a hand-picked hue breaks the one-accent rule. Evidence: app 96/96 call sites pass no colour class, and the 2 className uses set case, or figures and size at app/(app)/kitchen/board.tsx:310, read from the props of each <StatusBadge tag. Check: review.
  • Don't: <StatusBadge tone="neutral" className="bg-blue-100 text-blue-700">Online</StatusBadge>
  • Do: <StatusBadge tone="neutral">Online</StatusBadge>
  • rule/status-badge-not-a-button: When the person can change a record's state, put the control beside the badge, such as a RowAction, instead of making the badge clickable, because the badge is a span with no role, focus or keyboard path. Evidence: app 96/96 call sites render the badge as a plain label with no onClick. Check: review.
  • Don't: <span onClick={resolve}><StatusBadge domain="work" status="Open" /></span>
  • Do: <><StatusBadge domain="work" status="Open" /><RowAction tone="primary" onClick={resolve}>Resolve</RowAction></>

Limits

  • Not applicable: no break was measured this session. The badge sets whitespace-nowrap and shrink-0, so a label past the cell's width overflows instead of wrapping, and the longest real label was not probed at 390px.

Accessibility

Rests on a plain span. The status word is the text, so a screen reader reads the state inline with no extra markup. Contrast: NEEDS REVIEW. The comment at components/app/status-badge.tsx:8 says the warning tint keeps amber above 4.5:1 in light mode, and no tool measured it this session.

Textarea

Description

Textarea takes free text that runs past one line, such as notes for the kitchen or a reason for cancelling, and grows with what is typed.

import { Textarea } from "@/components/ui/textarea", source components/ui/textarea.tsx, status ready-with-gaps. Foundation: shadcn textarea (base-nova, base). Traps checked: trap/color-only-status (States: invalid shows the caller's error text, not only a red border), trap/reduced-motion-ignored n/a because only transition-colors runs, trap/motion-layout-property (Motion: colours only), trap/loading-layout-shift n/a because Textarea has no loading state, trap/decor-pointer n/a because Textarea draws no decoration.

Foundation

Given by the foundationAdded by the team
shadcn base-nova textarea: a native textarea with data-slot="textarea", field-sizing-content min-h-16, forwarding every textarea propThe field classes are copied from Input (rounded-lg, px-2.5, py-2, text-base md:text-sm, focus, disabled, invalid and dark styles) so a form's fields match

Examples

Default: docs/system/examples/textarea/default.tsx.

Real uses, 0 call sites. The app draws 14 raw native textareas instead (rg -n '<textarea' app components lib --glob '*.tsx'), such as app/(app)/kitchen/job-form-sections.tsx:168, app/(app)/engagement/enquiry-form.tsx:50 and app/(app)/suppliers/supplier-form.tsx:160. Each one rebuilds the field look from an input class plus its own height. Moving them onto Textarea is migration work, not part of this spec.

State precedence

  • Invalid and focus visible: both show. The ring is red.
  • Disabled and filled: both show. The text stays readable at 50% opacity.
  • Empty and filled: filled wins. The placeholder goes when text is typed.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Focus, blur or a change of invalid stateinputtransition-colors, Tailwind's 150ms default, no named presetbackground-color, border-color, colorNot handled, a 150ms colour fade only (NEEDS REVIEW)

Props

No props of its own.

Also accepts: native element attributes from React's types.

gen-docs writes the table from React.ComponentProps<'textarea'>. Textarea adds no props of its own.

  • className: overrides the field classes, such as a taller min-h-28 for a long message.

Usage

When to use

  • Free text that may run past one line, such as notes, a reason, a description or a message.

When not to use

  • A single line of text, such as a name, or a date. Use DateField instead for a date, and the single-line components/ui/input.tsx field (not in the registry yet) for the rest.
  • A fixed set of answers. Use Select instead.

Rules

  • Not applicable: Textarea has 0 call sites, so no rule has app evidence yet. The raw-textarea migration (G-04) brings the first ones.

Content

  • Not applicable: Textarea renders no text of its own. The label and placeholder are the caller's, in sentence case, such as "Notes for the kitchen".

Anti-slop

  • Not applicable: no rule has app evidence yet. The 14 raw native textareas are counted under Examples.

Limits

  • Not applicable: no length limit is built in. Callers pass maxLength, 500 or 2000 at today's raw call sites.

Accessibility

Rests on a native textarea, which takes focus, reads its value and joins forms with no extra work. It has no visible name of its own, so the caller joins a Label with id and htmlFor, or passes aria-label, and ties error text with aria-describedby.
